527	## D-023 — Frontend type strategy (hand-written types.ts with compile-time drift gate)
528	
529	**Decision.**
530	Per STRUCTURE §4, each frontend module keeps a HAND-WRITTEN `src/modules/<module>/types.ts` mirroring that module's backend Pydantic Read/Create/Update/Filter schemas, snake_case preserved (no camelCase translation layer).
531	
532	**Mapping conventions, fixed:** Decimal/money → `string`; date/datetime → `string` (ISO 8601); UUID → `string`; backend enums → TS string-literal unions of the UPPER_SNAKE values (`type EntryStatus = 'DRAFT' | 'POSTED' | 'REVERSED'`); nullable/Optional → `| null`; Masked fields → `T | null`. Shared envelope types (`Page<T> {items, next_cursor, limit}`, `ApiError {error: {code, message, details, request_id}}`) live once in `src/lib/apiClient.ts`.
533	
534	**Drift control, two compile-time gates and zero runtime cost:**
535	
536	1. `backend/openapi.json` is COMMITTED and regenerated via a Makefile target (`make openapi` calls a tiny dump entry that instantiates the app factory and writes `app.openapi()`); a backend pytest test asserts the committed file equals the live app's schema, so any schema change that forgets regeneration fails the backend CI job with a "run make openapi" message.
537	2. A frontend devDependency `openapi-typescript` generates a GITIGNORED `src/lib/openapi.gen.d.ts` from `../backend/openapi.json` as a pre-step of `npm run typecheck`; each module adds a `types.contract.ts` containing only type-level assertions using Expect/Equal helpers from lib (`type _ = Expect<Equal<JournalEntry, components['schemas']['JournalEntryRead']>>`) — one line per mirrored type — so tsc fails on any divergence in either direction.
538	
539	Application code imports ONLY the hand-written `types.ts`; the generated file is referenced solely by contract files and is never committed (consistent with STRUCTURE §8.6: generated files are never hand-edited; here it is also never shipped). The CI frontend job's existing `npm run typecheck` therefore enforces the contract with no new job.
540	
541	**Rationale.**
542	STRUCTURE mandates hand-written mirrors, which keeps frontend types curated and readable — but hand-written without a gate guarantees drift. Routing the gate through the committed OpenAPI document gives an explicit, reviewable contract artifact whose own freshness is enforced backend-side, while the type-level Equal assertions catch field renames, nullability changes, and enum-value drift at compile time in both directions. String-typed money/dates align with the backend's Decimal-as-string serialization and force all formatting through `lib/format.ts` per STRUCTURE.
543	
544	**Rejected alternatives.**
545	- Fully generated committed types as the app's source: violates the hand-written mandate, bloats diffs, and produces unidiomatic deeply-nested component types.
546	- Runtime zod/valibot validation: a second schema source to keep in sync and runtime cost on every response; the API is first-party so compile-time checking suffices.
547	- No gate ("be careful"): drift is guaranteed across 13 modules.
548	- Comparing types via a custom AST script: reimplements what tsc's structural equality already does.
549	
550	**Risks & mitigations.**
551	- `openapi.json` merge conflicts on parallel schema work — resolved by regenerating (`make openapi`), never hand-merging.
552	- Contract files add one assertion line per type — trivial, and a missing assertion is visible in review because the convention is one contract file per module listed beside `types.ts`.
553	- `Equal<>` on very large unions can slow tsc marginally — bounded by module-scoped contract files.

557	## D-024 — Frontend auth: in-memory access token, cookie refresh, cross-tab single-flight
558	
559	**Decision.**
560	`src/lib/auth.ts` owns all token state. **Access token:** held ONLY in a module-scoped variable (with a subscribe hook for React state) — never localStorage/sessionStorage. **Refresh token:** never touched by JS (httpOnly cookie managed by the browser, scoped to `/api/v1/auth` per D-008). `apiClient.ts` attaches `Authorization: Bearer` from auth.ts on every call.
561	
562	- **Boot sequence:** app start calls `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh` once (cookie present → new access+refresh pair, resumes the session silently; 401 → unauthenticated state, router redirects to /login).
563	- **Proactive renewal:** auth.ts decodes the access token's exp claim client-side (base64 decode only, no verification — it is not a trust decision) and schedules a refresh at exp minus 60 s.
564	- **Reactive path:** on any 401, apiClient triggers a single-flight refresh — within a tab, concurrent requests await one shared in-flight promise then retry exactly once; a second 401 after retry → hard logout.
565	- **Cross-tab coordination** (required because backend rotation invalidates the old refresh jti — even with the 10 s grace window, uncoordinated tabs hammering refresh is wrong): the refresher acquires `navigator.locks.request('atlas-auth-refresh')` so exactly one tab rotates, and broadcasts the new access token via `BroadcastChannel('atlas-auth')`; other tabs adopt it instead of refreshing; logout events broadcast the same way so all tabs clear state and redirect together.
566	- **Logout:** `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` (revokes the sid row, clears the cookie), clear memory, broadcast, `queryClient.clear()`.
567	- **Identity/permissions:** after any successful login/refresh-boot, fetch `GET /api/v1/auth/me` (user, tenant, permission keys) into TanStack Query; TanStack Router `beforeLoad` guards check auth.ts state and the permission set for route gating — UI-only convenience, the server remains the enforcement point.
568	- **Tenant selection** happens at login (tenant_slug field); the SPA never sends tenant headers — tenancy rides the JWT.
569	
570	**Rationale.**
571	Memory-only access tokens are XSS-resistant (no persistent readable storage) and the boot-refresh makes hard reloads seamless since the httpOnly cookie persists. Single-flight + Web Locks + BroadcastChannel is the standard answer to rotation-with-reuse-detection in multi-tab SPAs: it eliminates the benign-race family revocations the backend grace window only softens. Proactive renewal avoids latency spikes and thundering 401 retries. Keeping every fetch in apiClient.ts (per STRUCTURE) means the 401/retry/refresh logic exists exactly once.
572	
573	**Rejected alternatives.**
574	- localStorage/sessionStorage tokens: XSS-exfiltratable, explicitly rejected.
575	- Access token in a cookie too: makes every API call CSRF-relevant instead of just /auth.
576	- Per-tab independent refresh without coordination: races rotation and logs users out under normal multi-tab use.
577	- Service-worker token broker: strictly more moving parts for the same isolation in a v1 SPA.
578	- Storing permissions in localStorage for instant boot: stale-permission UI and another sync problem — /auth/me is one cheap request.
579	
580	**Risks & mitigations.**
581	- `navigator.locks`/BroadcastChannel need modern browsers — fine for v1 scope; a no-op fallback (per-tab single-flight only) keeps Safari/old engines working with the backend grace window absorbing the residual race.
582	- In-memory token dies on reload — by design; boot refresh restores it.
583	- Clock skew breaks proactive scheduling — harmless: the reactive 401 path is the safety net.
584

587	## D-025 — Backend testing strategy (async fixtures, per-test DB copies, trigger tests on SQLite)
588	
589	**Decision.**
590	pytest + pytest-asyncio with `asyncio_mode=auto`; HTTP tests use `httpx.AsyncClient` over `ASGITransport(app)` — no live server.
591	
592	**Database isolation uses the TEMPLATE-COPY pattern**, deliberately replacing the draft's SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction approach, which breaks the moment code under test performs REAL commits — and ours does by design (idempotency's separate reservation transaction, `run_in_uow` commits, numbering claims): a session-scoped fixture builds ONE migrated template SQLite file via programmatic `alembic.command.upgrade(config, 'head')` (env.py's `asyncio.run` pattern works because the session fixture runs outside any event loop); a function-scoped fixture copies that file (`shutil.copy`, ~ms) into tmp_path, builds an aiosqlite engine on the copy with the connect-event `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, and overrides the app's session dependency. Every test gets a fully migrated, trigger-bearing, fresh database where real commits are allowed and nothing leaks across tests. For the pg-marked subset in CI, a fixture creates a per-test database via `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE atlas_test_template` from a once-migrated template database and drops it after — same semantics on Postgres.
593	
594	**Fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`:** `tenant_factory` provisions tenant + admin user + role with named permissions through the REAL provisioning service under `system_context`, returning a handle with tenant_id and an `auth_headers(user)` helper that performs a real login; `authed_client` composes it; `permissions_context` sets the `current_permissions` ContextVar for serializer-level masking tests; module fixtures live in `tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py` per STRUCTURE §6.
595	
596	**DB-guard tests** (`tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py` etc.) deliberately use raw `session.execute(text(...))` to BYPASS the service layer — sanctioned because the CI grep gate banning `text()` is scoped to `app/`, not `tests/` — asserting that UPDATE/DELETE on posted lines, unbalanced DRAFT→POSTED, closed-period posting, and audit UPDATE/DELETE all raise with the `ATLAS_` tokens on SQLite, with the same tests re-run on Postgres via `-m pg`. The tenancy suite enumerates `Base.registry.mappers` (auto-covering new models); event-bus tests assert handler effects and rollback-on-handler-failure within one transaction; idempotency tests exercise the two-transaction reservation flow with real commits; determinism comes from explicit posting_date/anchor arguments in factories, not clock freezing.
597	
598	**Rationale.**
599	The template-copy pattern is the single decision that makes everything else testable as designed: SAVEPOINT isolation silently converts the idempotency guard's real COMMIT into a savepoint release (changing the very semantics under test) and shares state when code opens a second session. File copies are milliseconds on SQLite and CREATE DATABASE TEMPLATE is fast on Postgres, so the cost is negligible while every test sees the exact schema migrations produce — triggers included, which is the whole point of asserting DB guards in CI. Factories going through real services means tenancy stamping, numbering, docflow, and audit are exercised by every test that touches data.
600	
601	**Rejected alternatives.**
602	- SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction per test (the draft): incompatible with real multi-transaction code paths and second sessions; rejected as the primary pattern.
603	- `create_all` + trigger fixture: duplicates DDL outside migrations and tests a schema nobody ships.
604	- In-memory `:memory:` SQLite: cannot be shared across connections/sessions the way the app's engine needs, and cannot be template-copied.
605	- One shared DB with truncation between tests: ordering-sensitive and slow on Postgres.
606	
607	**Risks & mitigations.**
608	- Session-scoped template means schema changes require fixture cache invalidation — the template path embeds the Alembic head revision in its filename, so a new revision automatically rebuilds.
609	- Per-test PG database creation is slower (~100 ms each) — confined to the small pg-marked subset.
610	- Raw-SQL bypass tests are tightly coupled to trigger names/tokens — intentional pinning; they exist to fail when guards change.
611

614	## D-026 — Seed-data architecture (deterministic, per-template, three months of linked transactions)
615	
616	**Decision.**
617	`backend/seed.py` is a CLI (argparse: `--templates` defaulting to all five industry templates, `--anchor-date` defaulting to today, `--reset`) that assumes a migrated database (Makefile target chains `alembic upgrade head`).
618	
619	**Determinism:** one `random.Random(f'{template}:{anchor_date}')` per tenant — identical output for a given (template, anchor) pair; the anchor is recorded on the tenant so reruns are reproducible for bug reports.
620	
621	**Provisioning phase** under `system_context()`: per template, create tenant (slug `demo-<template>`, fixed admin credentials sourced from `.env.example` values), apply the YAML industry template via the industry module's real application service — modules toggled, display labels, chart-of-accounts preset, tax codes, number-sequence patterns, system roles, custom-field defs (written through `core/custom_fields.py`).
622	
623	**Transaction phase:** set the tenancy ContextVar to the tenant (NOT `system_context` — business writes must be stamped and filtered normally) and drive everything through the REAL service layer wrapped in `run_in_uow()`, never raw inserts — so numbering, docflow registration and links, domain events (goods issue → COGS), audit rows, and DB triggers all fire exactly as in production, making seed a standing integration proof.
624	
625	**Script per template spans 3 calendar months ending at anchor:** master data first (items, vendors, customers, warehouses, employees, WBS elements, exchange rates including one foreign currency); then interlinked flows — procurement P2P chains (requisition → PO → goods receipt → AP invoice → payment run), sales O2C (quote → order → delivery → customer invoice → receipt, including partial shipments and one open backorder), template-specific depth (production orders with WIP postings for manufacturing; projects + timesheets for professional-services; maintenance orders for construction; quality inspection lots for healthcare/retail receiving), foreign-currency invoices plus a month-end FX revaluation run, manual journal entries, and month-end closes: periods for months 1 and 2 CLOSED via the real period-close service, month 3 left OPEN with open AP/AR items so aging, dunning, and dashboards have live data. Volumes ~100-300 documents per tenant (seconds on SQLite).
626	
627	**Idempotency:** without `--reset`, seed refuses if a demo tenant exists; `--reset` hard-deletes the demo tenants by cascade — the ONLY sanctioned hard-delete path in the codebase, running under `system_context` and documented as such.
628	
629	**Self-verification:** seed ends by asserting, per tenant, (a) trial balance debits == credits, (b) every created document's docflow chain traverses end-to-end, (c) inventory GL balance == sum of `inv_item_valuations` — and CI runs seed against SQLite after the test suite as a smoke gate.
630	
631	**Rationale.**
632	Seeding through real services is the load-bearing choice: SQL-dump seeds rot with every migration and bypass exactly the invariants (gapless numbers, docflow, COGS events, period triggers) the demo exists to showcase, while service-driven seeding doubles as an end-to-end integration test the CI runs for free. Deterministic RNG + recorded anchor gives reproducible demos and bug reports without freezing real time. Closing two of three months demonstrates the period-close machinery and leaves believable open items for the operational screens.
633	
634	**Rejected alternatives.**
635	- SQL dump / fixtures files: bypass invariants, drift with schema, undebuggable diffs.
636	- Faker with random seed-per-run: non-reproducible demo states.
637	- Seeding via HTTP API: needs a running server and auth choreography for zero added fidelity — the service layer is the contract.
638	- A full year of data: slower seeds for no demo value; the parity scope's reports all read well at 3 months.
639	
640	**Risks & mitigations.**
641	- Anchor defaulting to today means runs on different days differ in dates (structure stays identical given anchor) — acceptable; CI pins a fixed anchor for the smoke gate.
642	- Seed duration creeps as modules land — bounded by per-tenant volume caps and the CI timing check.
643	- The `--reset` cascade is a footgun if pointed at a non-demo tenant — guarded by a slug prefix check (refuses anything not starting with `demo-`).

1	"""Inventory master data (PLAN 5.1): item categories, UoMs, per-item UoM conversions, the item
2	master, and the lot/serial instance tables.
3	
4	Single ``models.py`` (STRUCTURE §3: split into a models/ package only at the 400-line cap, the
5	finance precedent). Six tables, all under that for 5.1.
6	
7	Design decisions baked in here:
8	
9	- **Costing wiring on the category (D-020 + D-029).** ``ItemCategory`` carries the default
10	  costing method AND the three GL accounts COGS/valuation posting will need —
11	  ``inventory_account_id``, ``cogs_account_id``, ``price_difference_account_id`` — as OPAQUE
12	  ``sa.Uuid`` columns, NOT cross-module FKs (D-029): finance owns those accounts; the inventory
13	  service validates each id exists via ``finance/queries.py`` when set, and the journal-line
14	  precedent already stores finance dimension ids without an FK on a cross-module table. They are
15	  NULLABLE on the category (a SERVICE-only category needs none); a STOCKED item's category must
16	  carry them before that item can post moves — validated when moves land (5.2+), not in 5.1.
17	
18	- **costing_method on the item (D-020).** Defaulted from the category at create but STORED on the
19	  item, because the item is the costing unit and D-020 lets it change only while no stock exists.
20	
21	- **UoM convention (the chosen one of the two the task offered): per-item BASE + ALTERNATES.**
22	  Each item has ONE ``base_uom_id``; quantities are stored/costed in the base UoM. An
23	  ``UomConversion`` row expresses an ALTERNATE UoM for that item as ``factor_to_base`` —
24	  multiplying a quantity in the alternate UoM by the factor yields the base-UoM quantity (an
25	  item whose base is EA and has BOX with factor 12 means 1 BOX = 12 EA). ``UNIQUE(tenant_id,
26	  item_id, alt_uom_id)`` — one factor per (item, alternate). This is the standard ERP shape
27	  (S/4HANA's alternative-UoM table): simpler than a full from/to graph, and base<->alt and
28	  alt<->alt conversions all derive from the single per-alternate factor (service.convert_quantity).
29	
30	- **Lot / SerialNumber are MASTER tables only for 5.1.** They are defined so the schema is
31	  receipt-ready, but instances are CREATED during receipts (5.2+); 5.1 ships no CRUD for them.
32	
33	All tables follow the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop: ``tenant_unique()`` on every table
34	referenced by a child, ``tenant_fk()`` composites for every cross-row link so a child can never
35	point at another tenant's parent. Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the
36	StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value (the core/finance convention, no ``sa.Enum``); the service maps
37	to/from the constants classes.

1	"""Inventory's cross-module read interface (STRUCTURE §5).
2	
3	Inventory sits just above finance in the dependency order: every module above it (procurement,
4	sales, manufacturing) may import THIS file to read inventory state synchronously, and inventory
5	imports only finance/queries downward. Keep this surface thin and stable — it is a contract; it is
6	the ONLY inventory file other modules import.
7	
8	For PLAN 5.1 it exposes the item-master reads those modules will need: existence checks, the
9	item's base UoM and costing method, and the category's GL-account wiring (so the COGS handler can
10	resolve where to post when stock issues land in 5.2+). Stock on-hand/availability reads join here
11	once moves exist (5.2+).
12	
13	Every function takes an explicit ``tenant_id`` and runs under the caller's tenant context, so the
14	D-007 filter applies on top of the explicit predicate — ordinary tenant-scoped reads, not a bypass.
15	"""
16	
17	import uuid
18	
19	from sqlalchemy import select
20	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
21	
22	from app.modules.inventory.constants import CostingMethod
23	from app.modules.inventory.models import Item, ItemCategory
24	
25	
26	async def get_item(
27	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
28	) -> Item | None:

9	tenant-scoped collection ETag (PERFORMANCE §3 / D-035): an If-None-Match hit returns 304 without
10	running the page query. Items are semi-reference data (they change less than transactions), so the

55	async def _commit[T](session: SessionDep, work: Callable[[], Awaitable[T]]) -> T:
56	    """Run a service call inside the D-011 uow, returning its ORM result refreshed in the async
57	    context so a sync ``model_validate`` never trips MissingGreenlet (twin of finance _commit)."""
58	    holder: list[T] = []

4	raise); category + base UoM exist; costing_method defaults from the category when omitted (D-020),

26	def _resolve_tracking(item_type: ItemType, tracking_mode: TrackingMode) -> None:
27	    """Enforce "tracking only on STOCKED items" (D-020): a NON_STOCKED/SERVICE item must keep
28	    tracking_mode = NONE — those types carry no stock to track."""
29	    if item_type != ItemType.STOCKED and tracking_mode != TrackingMode.NONE:
30	        raise ValidationFailedError(
31	            message="Only stocked items can be lot- or serial-tracked",
32	            code="inventory.tracking_requires_stocked",
33	            details={"item_type": item_type.value, "tracking_mode": tracking_mode.value},
34	        )

39	    if item is None or item.tenant_id != tenant_id:
40	        raise NotFoundError(message="Item not found", code="inventory.item_not_found")

44	async def create_item(
45	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: ItemCreate
46	) -> Item:
47	    """Create an item. Validates the category + base UoM exist, defaults costing_method from the
48	    category when omitted (D-020), and enforces tracking-only-on-stocked. Duplicate item_code →
49	    ConflictError (the DB UNIQUE is the backstop)."""
50	    existing = (
51	        await session.execute(
52	            select(Item.id).where(
53	                Item.tenant_id == tenant_id, Item.item_code == payload.item_code
54	            )
55	        )
56	    ).first()
57	    if existing is not None:
58	        raise ConflictError(
59	            message=f"An item with code {payload.item_code} already exists",
60	            code="inventory.item_code_conflict",
61	            details={"item_code": payload.item_code},
62	        )
63	    category = await get_category(session, tenant_id, payload.category_id)
64	    await get_uom(session, tenant_id, payload.base_uom_id)
65	
66	    item_type = ItemType(payload.item_type)
67	    tracking_mode = TrackingMode(payload.tracking_mode)
68	    _resolve_tracking(item_type, tracking_mode)
69	    costing_method = (
70	        CostingMethod(payload.costing_method)
71	        if payload.costing_method is not None
72	        else CostingMethod(category.default_costing_method)
73	    )
74	    item = Item(
75	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
76	        item_code=payload.item_code,
77	        name=payload.name,
78	        description=payload.description,
79	        item_type=item_type.value,
80	        category_id=payload.category_id,
81	        base_uom_id=payload.base_uom_id,
82	        costing_method=costing_method.value,
83	        tracking_mode=tracking_mode.value,
84	        is_active=payload.is_active,
85	        reorder_point=payload.reorder_point,
86	        reorder_quantity=payload.reorder_quantity,
87	    )

95	) -> Item:
96	    """Partial update of an item (D-010: mutate the loaded object). item_code and item_type are
97	    immutable and absent from the schema; a changed category/base UoM is re-validated and a changed
98	    tracking_mode is re-checked against the (immutable) item_type."""
99	    item = await get_item(session, tenant_id, item_id)
100	    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
101	    if data.get("category_id") is not None:
102	        await get_category(session, tenant_id, data["category_id"])
103	    if data.get("base_uom_id") is not None:
104	        await get_uom(session, tenant_id, data["base_uom_id"])
105	    if data.get("tracking_mode") is not None:
106	        _resolve_tracking(ItemType(item.item_type), TrackingMode(data["tracking_mode"]))
107	        data["tracking_mode"] = TrackingMode(data["tracking_mode"]).value
108	    if data.get("costing_method") is not None:
109	        data["costing_method"] = CostingMethod(data["costing_method"]).value
110	    for field, value in data.items():
111	        setattr(item, field, value)
112	    await session.flush()
113	    return item

124	    """Keyset-paginated item list ordered by item_code (D-014). Filters (type/category/active)

136	    )

139	        stmt,
140	        order_by=[OrderKey(Item.item_code, SortDirection.ASC)],
141	        pk=Item.id,
142	        cursor=cursor,
143	        limit=limit,
144	        filters=fingerprint,
145	    )

1	"""Per-item UoM-conversion business logic + the pure ``convert_quantity`` helper (PLAN 5.1).
2	
3	The chosen UoM convention (per-item base + alternates): each item has one base UoM, and a
4	conversion expresses an ALTERNATE UoM as ``factor_to_base`` — multiplying an alternate-UoM quantity
5	by the factor yields the base-UoM quantity. ``convert_quantity`` is a PURE function over a loaded
6	factor table, so it is fully unit-testable and reused by stock moves later (PLAN 5.2+).
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import uuid
12	from decimal import Decimal
13	
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
16	
17	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, ValidationFailedError
18	from app.modules.inventory.models import UomConversion
19	from app.modules.inventory.schemas import UomConversionCreate
20	from app.modules.inventory.service.items import get_item
21	from app.modules.inventory.service.uoms import get_uom
22	
23	# Quantization quantum for converted quantities: scale 6, matching QuantityType storage (D-015).
24	_QUANTITY_QUANTUM = Decimal(10) ** -6
25	
26	
27	async def create_conversion(
28	    session: AsyncSession,
29	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
30	    item_id: uuid.UUID,
31	    payload: UomConversionCreate,
32	) -> UomConversion:
33	    """Add an alternate UoM for an item (PLAN 5.1). Validates the item + alternate UoM exist, that
34	    the alternate is not the item's base UoM, and that the factor is positive (mirrors the DB
35	    CHECK). A duplicate (item, alternate) → ConflictError (the DB UNIQUE is the backstop)."""
36	    item = await get_item(session, tenant_id, item_id)
37	    await get_uom(session, tenant_id, payload.alt_uom_id)
38	    if payload.alt_uom_id == item.base_uom_id:
39	        raise ValidationFailedError(
40	            message="The alternate UoM cannot be the item's base UoM",
41	            code="inventory.conversion_alt_is_base",
42	        )
43	    if payload.factor_to_base <= 0:
44	        raise ValidationFailedError(
45	            message="The conversion factor must be greater than zero",
46	            code="inventory.conversion_factor_invalid",
47	        )
48	    existing = (
49	        await session.execute(
50	            select(UomConversion.id).where(
51	                UomConversion.tenant_id == tenant_id,
52	                UomConversion.item_id == item_id,
53	                UomConversion.alt_uom_id == payload.alt_uom_id,
54	            )
55	        )
56	    ).first()
57	    if existing is not None:
58	        raise ConflictError(
59	            message="A conversion for this alternate UoM already exists on the item",
60	            code="inventory.conversion_conflict",
61	        )
62	    conversion = UomConversion(
63	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
64	        item_id=item_id,
65	        alt_uom_id=payload.alt_uom_id,
66	        factor_to_base=payload.factor_to_base,
67	    )
68	    session.add(conversion)
69	    await session.flush()
70	    return conversion
71	
72	
73	async def list_conversions(
74	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
75	) -> list[UomConversion]:
76	    """All alternate-UoM conversions for an item, ordered by id for stable output. The item must
77	    exist (404 otherwise). The set is small (a handful of alternates per item), so it is returned
78	    whole rather than paginated."""
79	    await get_item(session, tenant_id, item_id)
80	    stmt = (
81	        select(UomConversion)
82	        .where(UomConversion.tenant_id == tenant_id, UomConversion.item_id == item_id)
83	        .order_by(UomConversion.id)
84	    )
85	    return list((await session.execute(stmt)).scalars().all())
86	
87	
88	async def get_conversion_factors(
89	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, item_id: uuid.UUID
90	) -> dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal]:
91	    """Map of alt_uom_id -> factor_to_base for an item (PLAN 5.1). The base UoM maps to factor 1.
92	    Loaded once so ``convert_quantity`` is a pure function over the resulting table — the shape
93	    stock moves (5.2+) reuse when converting a document line's UoM to the item's base."""
94	    item = await get_item(session, tenant_id, item_id)
95	    conversions = await list_conversions(session, tenant_id, item_id)
96	    factors: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal] = {item.base_uom_id: Decimal(1)}
97	    for conversion in conversions:
98	        factors[conversion.alt_uom_id] = Decimal(str(conversion.factor_to_base))
99	    return factors
100	
101	
102	def convert_quantity(
103	    quantity: Decimal,
104	    from_uom_id: uuid.UUID,
105	    to_uom_id: uuid.UUID,
106	    base_uom_id: uuid.UUID,
107	    factors: dict[uuid.UUID, Decimal],
108	) -> Decimal:
109	    """Convert ``quantity`` from ``from_uom_id`` to ``to_uom_id`` for one item — PURE (no I/O), so
110	    it is fully unit-testable and reused by stock moves later (PLAN 5.2+).
111	
112	    Convention: ``factors[u]`` is u's factor-to-base (base maps to 1). A quantity in any UoM ``u``
113	    equals ``quantity * factors[u]`` base units; dividing by the target's factor lands it in the
114	    target UoM. So base<->alt and alt<->alt both fall out of the single per-alternate factor:
115	    ``to_qty = quantity * factors[from] / factors[to]``. Result quantizes to scale 6 (QuantityType
116	    storage, D-015). An unknown UoM for this item raises — conversions are per item, so a UoM with
117	    no factor is not convertible against this item."""
118	    for uom_id in (from_uom_id, to_uom_id):
119	        if uom_id not in factors:
120	            raise ValidationFailedError(
121	                message="No conversion is defined for this UoM on the item",
122	                code="inventory.conversion_undefined",
123	                details={"uom_id": str(uom_id), "base_uom_id": str(base_uom_id)},
124	            )
125	    if from_uom_id == to_uom_id:
126	        return Decimal(quantity).quantize(_QUANTITY_QUANTUM)
127	    base_quantity = Decimal(quantity) * factors[from_uom_id]
128	    return (base_quantity / factors[to_uom_id]).quantize(_QUANTITY_QUANTUM)

1	"""D-012 gapless per-tenant document numbering.
2	
3	One half of the merged registry+numbering subsystem (the other half is core/docflow.py).
4	A document number is claimed INSIDE the business transaction that makes the document
5	permanent (drafts are numbered at posting). Because the counter increment and the
6	document insert commit or roll back together, gaplessness for committed documents falls
7	out of ACID with no burned-number reconciliation state (D-012 claim-timing rule).
8	
9	The atomic claim is a single ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
10	... RETURNING next_value`` — one portable statement that takes the row lock and reads the
11	new counter in one round trip. RETURNING is verified working on the project's aiosqlite
12	(SQLite >= 3.35; this build runs 3.53) and on Postgres, so no SELECT-then-UPDATE fallback
13	is needed (D-012 sanctioned the fallback only if RETURNING were unavailable).
14	
15	The ORM model lives HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is at ~273 lines and
16	adding the numbering + docflow entities would push it over the ~350-line soft cap, so the
17	D-012 entities sit in their concern files (numbering.py / docflow.py) — a placement the
18	PLAN sanctions explicitly and STRUCTURE §2 permits ("one concept per file": the sequence
19	concept lives with its claim logic). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
20	"""
21	
22	import uuid
23	from datetime import date
24	
25	import sqlalchemy as sa
26	from sqlalchemy import select
27	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
28	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
29	
30	from app.core.exceptions import NotFoundError
31	from app.core.models import (
32	    Base,
33	    TenantMixin,
34	    TimestampMixin,
35	    UuidPKMixin,
36	    tenant_fk,
37	)
38	
39	
40	class NumberSequence(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
41	    """Per-tenant gapless counter for one document kind (D-012).
42	
43	    ``name`` is the namespaced sequence key (e.g. ``'finance.invoice'``); a claim formats
44	    ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded next_value}`` (e.g. ``INV-2026-00001``). When ``year_reset``
45	    is set the running number restarts at 1 each calendar year and the year segment is
46	    rendered; ``current_year`` records which year the counter currently belongs to so the
47	    first claim of a new year resets it on demand (no rollover job, per D-012). Not
48	    AuditMixin: sequence rows are infrastructure counters mutated on every claim, not
49	    business state — auditing every increment would be noise (documented exclusion)."""
50	
51	    __tablename__ = "core_number_sequences"
52	    __table_args__ = (
53	        # One sequence per (tenant, name). Explicit name: the D-022 convention keys on
54	        # column 0 (tenant_id) only and would collide with tenant_unique() below.
55	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "name", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id_name"),
56	        # UNIQUE(tenant_id, id) so other tenant-scoped tables could reference a sequence via
57	        # the composite-FK backstop if ever needed (D-007 item 4).
58	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_number_sequences_tenant_id"),
59	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
60	    )
61	
62	    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
63	    prefix: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(20), nullable=False)
64	    padding: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
65	    # Next number to hand out. The atomic claim does next_value = next_value + 1 RETURNING
66	    # the post-increment value, so the FIRST claim of a sequence at next_value=1 returns 1.
67	    next_value: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
68	        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=1, server_default=sa.text("1")
69	    )
70	    year_reset: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
71	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
72	    )
73	    # The year the running counter belongs to (NULL when year_reset is off).
74	    current_year: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=True)
75	
76	
77	def _format_number(prefix: str, padding: int, value: int, year: int | None) -> str:
78	    """Render ``{prefix}-{year?}-{padded value}`` — the year segment is present only when
79	    the sequence year-resets (D-012). e.g. ('INV', 5, 1, 2026) -> 'INV-2026-00001'."""
80	    padded = str(value).zfill(padding)
81	    if year is None:
82	        return f"{prefix}-{padded}"
83	    return f"{prefix}-{year}-{padded}"
84	
85	
86	async def ensure_sequence(
87	    session: AsyncSession,
88	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
89	    name: str,
90	    prefix: str,
91	    padding: int,
92	    year_reset: bool,
93	) -> NumberSequence:
94	    """Idempotent creator for provisioning/seed (D-012: year rollover and sequence setup
95	    need no job — the row is created on demand). Returns the existing row unchanged if the
96	    (tenant, name) sequence already exists, otherwise inserts it at next_value=1.
97	
98	    A Core insert is used (not an ORM add) so the tenant_id is set explicitly and the row
99	    is not subject to ORM tenant stamping — consistent with the D-007 sanction that core/
100	    numbering writes carry tenant_id explicitly. Callers run under the target tenant context
101	    or system_context (provisioning)."""
102	    existing = (
103	        await session.execute(
104	            select(NumberSequence).where(
105	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
106	            )
107	        )
108	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
109	    if existing is not None:
110	        return existing
111	
112	    current_year = date.today().year if year_reset else None
113	    await session.execute(
114	        sa.insert(NumberSequence.__table__).values(
115	            id=uuid.uuid4(),
116	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
117	            name=name,
118	            prefix=prefix,
119	            padding=padding,
120	            next_value=1,
121	            year_reset=year_reset,
122	            current_year=current_year,
123	        )
124	    )
125	    return (
126	        await session.execute(
127	            select(NumberSequence).where(
128	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == name
129	            )
130	        )
131	    ).scalar_one()
132	
133	
134	async def claim_number(
135	    session: AsyncSession,
136	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
137	    sequence_name: str,
138	    *,
139	    on_date: date,
140	) -> str:
141	    """Atomically claim the next number for ``sequence_name`` and return the formatted
142	    string (D-012). The claim runs in the CALLER's transaction — the number is permanent
143	    only when that transaction commits, so a rollback returns the value to the pool and the
144	    next committed claim reuses it (gaplessness for committed documents).
145	
146	    Mechanism — one portable atomic statement per claim:
147	    ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
148	      WHERE tenant_id=:t AND name=:n RETURNING next_value`` — the RETURNING value is the
149	    post-increment counter; the row lock the UPDATE takes serializes concurrent claimers so
150	    two claims can never read the same number (verified on aiosqlite >= 3.35 and Postgres).
151	
152	    Year reset (when ``year_reset``): if ``on_date.year`` differs from the stored
153	    ``current_year``, the counter is reset to 1 for the new year FIRST (a guarded UPDATE
154	    that only fires while current_year is still the old value, so a concurrent claimer that
155	    reset it already cannot double-reset), then the normal atomic increment claims 1.
156	
157	    A Core UPDATE is used (bypasses the ORM tenant filter by design — core/ numbering is a
158	    D-007 sanctioned raw-SQL site with explicit tenant_id)."""
159	    sequence = (
160	        await session.execute(
161	            select(NumberSequence).where(
162	                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == sequence_name
163	            )
164	        )
165	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
166	    if sequence is None:
167	        raise NotFoundError(
168	            message=f"Number sequence '{sequence_name}' is not configured for this tenant",
169	            code="core.number_sequence_missing",
170	        )
171	
172	    table = NumberSequence.__table__
173	    claim_year: int | None = None
174	    if sequence.year_reset:
175	        claim_year = on_date.year
176	        if sequence.current_year != claim_year:
177	            # Reset to 1 for the new year, guarded on the OLD current_year so a racing
178	            # claimer that already rolled the year over does not reset a second time.
179	            await session.execute(
180	                sa.update(table)
181	                .where(
182	                    table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
183	                    table.c.name == sequence_name,
184	                    table.c.current_year.is_not_distinct_from(sequence.current_year),
185	                )
186	                .values(next_value=1, current_year=claim_year)
187	            )
188	
189	    result = await session.execute(
190	        sa.update(table)
191	        .where(table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id, table.c.name == sequence_name)
192	        .values(next_value=table.c.next_value + 1)
193	        .returning(table.c.next_value)
194	    )
195	    next_after = result.scalar_one()
196	    claimed_value = next_after - 1
197	
198	    # The Core UPDATE changed the row out from under the loaded ORM object; expire it so its
199	    # attributes reload from the DB on next access rather than being marked dirty (which
200	    # would trigger a redundant ORM UPDATE on the next flush).
201	    formatted = _format_number(sequence.prefix, sequence.padding, claimed_value, claim_year)
202	    session.expire(sequence)
203	    return formatted

1	"""Declarative Base with the D-022 naming convention and shared model mixins."""
2	
3	import uuid
4	from datetime import UTC, datetime
5	from typing import Any
6	
7	import sqlalchemy as sa
8	from sqlalchemy.dialects import postgresql
9	from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, declared_attr, mapped_column
10	
11	# Deterministic constraint names are mandatory: SQLite batch-mode migrations
12	# cannot drop unnamed constraints (D-022).
13	NAMING_CONVENTION = {
14	    "ix": "ix_%(column_0_label)s",
15	    "uq": "uq_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s",
16	    "ck": "ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s",
17	    "fk": "fk_%(table_name)s_%(column_0_name)s_%(referred_table_name)s",
18	    "pk": "pk_%(table_name)s",
19	}
20	
21	# Portable JSON: JSONB on Postgres, plain JSON elsewhere. Type variance lives in
22	# the models so migrations import it from here and stay dialect-clean (D-022).
23	JSON_VARIANT = sa.JSON().with_variant(postgresql.JSONB(), "postgresql")
24	
25	
26	class Base(DeclarativeBase):
27	    metadata = sa.MetaData(naming_convention=NAMING_CONVENTION)
28	
29	
30	class UuidPKMixin:
31	    """uuid4 primary key, client-generated so ids are portable across both engines."""
32	
33	    id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, primary_key=True, default=uuid.uuid4)
34	
35	
36	class TenantMixin:
37	    """Row-level tenancy marker (D-007). Filtering and stamping are enforced by the
38	    core/tenancy.py session listeners; query authors never touch tenant_id."""
39	
40	    @declared_attr
41	    def tenant_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
42	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, index=True)
43	
44	
45	class AuditMixin:
46	    """Marker mixin (D-010): tags a model for split-phase audit capture. It adds NO
47	    columns — the audit listeners in core/audit.py test ``isinstance(obj, AuditMixin)``
48	    to decide which INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE flushes land in core_audit_log. Per-column
49	    opt-outs are declared on the model via ``__audit_exclude__`` (a frozenset of
50	    attribute names); ``password_hash`` is excluded there on User."""
51	
52	    # Attribute names never written to the diff (D-010: password_hash always). Models
53	    # override by setting their own frozenset; the listeners read it via getattr.
54	    __audit_exclude__: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
55	
56	
57	def utcnow() -> datetime:
58	    """Canonical timestamp source for every SQLAlchemy write (#34)."""
59	    return datetime.now(UTC)
60	
61	
62	class TimestampMixin:
63	    """Timezone-aware UTC stamps, ALWAYS Python-written (#34).
64	
65	    The Python ``default``/``onupdate`` fire for ORM and Core inserts alike, so every
66	    stored value uses SQLAlchemy's canonical SQLite string format (six-digit
67	    microseconds). The DDL ``server_default`` remains only as a fallback for raw SQL
68	    outside SQLAlchemy and must never be relied on: SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP writes
69	    second-precision strings whose lexicographic comparison against bound datetimes
70	    breaks keyset-pagination equality — the #34 infinite-page-loop bug."""
71	
72	    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
73	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
74	        nullable=False,
75	        default=utcnow,
76	        server_default=sa.func.now(),
77	    )
78	    updated_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
79	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True),
80	        nullable=False,
81	        default=utcnow,
82	        server_default=sa.func.now(),
83	        onupdate=utcnow,
84	    )
85	
86	
87	def tenant_fk(target_table: str, local_column: str | None = None) -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
88	    """Tenant-safe foreign key for __table_args__ (D-007 item 4).
89	
90	    - tenant_fk("adm_tenants") anchors tenant_id itself to the tenants root;
91	      every tenant-scoped table carries this backstop.
92	    - tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id") builds the composite (tenant_id, item_id)
93	      -> (inv_items.tenant_id, inv_items.id) FK, so a child row can never point
94	      at a parent row of another tenant; the parent declares tenant_unique().
95	    """
96	    if local_column is None:
97	        return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(["tenant_id"], [f"{target_table}.id"])
98	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
99	        ["tenant_id", local_column],
100	        [f"{target_table}.tenant_id", f"{target_table}.id"],
101	    )
102	
103	
104	def tenant_unique() -> sa.UniqueConstraint:
105	    """UNIQUE (tenant_id, id) — required on every tenant-scoped table that is
106	    referenced through tenant_fk() composite FKs (D-007 item 4). Any OTHER unique
107	    constraint starting with tenant_id needs an explicit name at the call site:
108	    the D-022 naming convention keys on column 0 only and would collide."""
109	    return sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id")
110	
111	
112	class User(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
113	    """Auth principal (D-008). Cross-cutting platform entity, so it lives in core
114	    (STRUCTURE §2 litmus: users are not a business concept). Provisioning is owned
115	    by modules/admin (PLAN 14); login lookup runs under system_context (D-007 site 1).
116	    HR compensation/PII masking is HR's concern later — these rows are credentials only.
117	    Audited (D-010): security-relevant; password_hash is excluded from every diff."""
118	
119	    __tablename__ = "core_users"
120	    # D-010: never write the credential into the audit diff (insert, update, or delete).
121	    __audit_exclude__ = frozenset({"password_hash"})
122	    __table_args__ = (
123	        # Explicit uq name: the D-022 convention keys on column 0 (tenant_id) only and
124	        # would collide with tenant_unique() below.
125	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "email", name="uq_core_users_tenant_id_email"),
126	        tenant_unique(),
127	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
128	    )
129	
130	    email: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(320), nullable=False)
131	    password_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(255), nullable=False)
132	    full_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=True)
133	    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
134	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()
135	    )
136	    # "Revoke everything" valve: bump this and every outstanding access token whose
137	    # `ver` claim no longer matches is rejected on its next request (D-008).
138	    token_version: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(
139	        sa.Integer, nullable=False, default=0, server_default=sa.text("0")
140	    )
141	
142	
143	class RefreshSession(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
144	    """Refresh-token server state (D-008). The PK id is the `sid` claim. Rotation is a
145	    compare-and-swap on current_jti_hash; prev_jti_hash + rotated_at implement the
146	    10-second grace window for benign multi-tab refresh races."""
147	
148	    __tablename__ = "core_refresh_sessions"
149	    __table_args__ = (
150	        tenant_unique(),
151	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
152	        tenant_fk("core_users", "user_id"),
153	        # Hot read path: refresh loads by sid (PK already), logout/revoke and the
154	        # "active sessions" admin view filter by user within a tenant.
155	        sa.Index("ix_core_refresh_sessions_tenant_id_user_id", "tenant_id", "user_id"),
156	    )
157	
158	    user_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
159	    current_jti_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(64), nullable=False)
160	    prev_jti_hash: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(64), nullable=True)
161	    rotated_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
162	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True
163	    )
164	    issued_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False)
165	    last_used_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False)

1	"""D-012 document registry, flow links, and chain traversal.
2	
3	The registry turns the polymorphic (doc_type, doc_id) problem into ordinary FK integrity:
4	every business document row links to exactly one ``core_documents`` registry entry via the
5	NOT NULL ``document_id`` FK supplied by ``DocumentMixin``. Predecessor/successor edges live
6	in ``core_doc_links``, so chain traversal is one generic recursive CTE over two narrow
7	tables — the ACDOCA-era Document Relationship Browser shape — with zero module-aware code in
8	core (core imports nothing from modules).
9	
10	Claim-timing (D-012): a document is registered with ``doc_number`` NULL at creation;
11	documents with a draft lifecycle are numbered at posting via the numbering claim, documents
12	permanent at creation are numbered immediately. The partial unique index on
13	``(tenant_id, doc_number)`` is the DB backstop turning any numbering bug into a constraint
14	violation.
15	
16	The ORM models live HERE rather than in core/models.py: models.py is near its ~350-line
17	soft cap, so the D-012 entities sit in their concern file (consistent with numbering.py and
18	sanctioned by the PLAN). Noted in DECISIONS.md.
19	"""
20	
21	import uuid
22	from dataclasses import dataclass
23	
24	import sqlalchemy as sa
25	from sqlalchemy import select
26	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
27	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, declared_attr, mapped_column
28	
29	from app.core.models import (
30	    Base,
31	    TenantMixin,
32	    TimestampMixin,
33	    UuidPKMixin,
34	    tenant_fk,
35	)
36	
37	# Depth ceiling on chain traversal (D-012): real chains are <10 nodes; the cap plus the
38	# visited-path cycle guard make a malformed graph terminate instead of spinning.
39	_MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH = 20
40	
41	
42	class Document(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
43	    """Registry entry for one business document (D-012). ``doc_type`` is a namespaced
44	    constant (``'sales.order'``, ``'finance.journal_entry'``) declared in module
45	    constants.py; ``doc_id`` is the PK of the business row in its own table; ``doc_number``
46	    is assigned at posting (NULL until then); ``status`` is the registry-level status string.
47	
48	    Not AuditMixin: the registry mirrors business rows that are themselves audited — the
49	    document's own table carries the audited business state, so auditing the registry too
50	    would double-record (documented exclusion)."""
51	
52	    __tablename__ = "core_documents"
53	    __table_args__ = (
54	        # One registry row per business document. Explicit name (D-022 convention keys on
55	        # column 0 only and would collide with tenant_unique()).
56	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
57	            "tenant_id", "doc_type", "doc_id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_type_doc_id"
58	        ),
59	        # Required so business rows can reference a registry entry via the composite tenant FK
60	        # (D-007 item 4) — DocumentMixin.document_fk() targets this.
61	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_documents_tenant_id"),
62	        # Partial unique index: a tenant may have many UNNUMBERED documents (doc_number NULL)
63	        # but never two with the SAME doc_number. Both dialect kwargs are required — Postgres
64	        # and SQLite each need their own (D-012 / D-021 dialect-kwargs pattern); a plain
65	        # UNIQUE would (incorrectly) reject multiple NULLs on some engines.
66	        sa.Index(
67	            "uq_core_documents_tenant_id_doc_number",
68	            "tenant_id",
69	            "doc_number",
70	            unique=True,
71	            postgresql_where=sa.text("doc_number IS NOT NULL"),
72	            sqlite_where=sa.text("doc_number IS NOT NULL"),
73	        ),
74	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
75	    )
76	
77	    doc_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(100), nullable=False)
78	    doc_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
79	    doc_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
80	    status: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)
81	
82	
83	class DocumentLink(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
84	    """A predecessor -> successor edge between two registry entries (D-012). ``link_type``
85	    names the relationship (``'fulfills'``, ``'invoices'``, ``'reverses'``, ``'posts'``).
86	    Both endpoints carry the composite tenant FK backstop so an edge can never span tenants.
87	    A CHECK forbids self-edges (a document cannot be its own predecessor)."""
88	
89	    __tablename__ = "core_doc_links"
90	    __table_args__ = (
91	        # One edge per (tenant, predecessor, successor). Explicit name (D-022 column-0 rule).
92	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
93	            "tenant_id",
94	            "predecessor_document_id",
95	            "successor_document_id",
96	            name="uq_core_doc_links_tenant_id_predecessor_document_id_successor",
97	        ),
98	        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "id", name="uq_core_doc_links_tenant_id"),
99	        # Pass the bare token: the D-022 ck convention wraps it as
100	        # ck_<table>_<constraint_name> -> ck_core_doc_links_no_self_link (matches 0006).
101	        sa.CheckConstraint(
102	            "predecessor_document_id != successor_document_id",
103	            name="no_self_link",
104	        ),
105	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
106	        # Both endpoints reference core_documents through the composite tenant FK, so the
107	        # D-022 column-0 convention would name both identically (collision). Spell out
108	        # distinct names that match migration 0006 exactly.
109	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
110	            ["tenant_id", "predecessor_document_id"],
111	            ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
112	            name="fk_core_doc_links_tenant_id_core_documents",
113	        ),
114	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
115	            ["tenant_id", "successor_document_id"],
116	            ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
117	            name="fk_core_doc_links_successor_document_id_core_documents",
118	        ),
119	    )
120	
121	    predecessor_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
122	    successor_document_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
123	    link_type: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=True)
124	
125	
126	def document_fk() -> sa.ForeignKeyConstraint:
127	    """Composite tenant-safe FK for a business table's ``document_id`` -> core_documents
128	    (D-007 item 4). A business model that mixes in DocumentMixin adds this to its
129	    __table_args__ so the link can never point at another tenant's registry row, mirroring
130	    the tenant_fk()/tenant_unique() pattern in core/models.py."""
131	    return sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
132	        ["tenant_id", "document_id"],
133	        ["core_documents.tenant_id", "core_documents.id"],
134	    )
135	
136	
137	class DocumentMixin:
138	    """Business-document link mixin (D-012). A business model mixes this in to get a NOT NULL
139	    ``document_id`` column tying its row to its registry entry — so the row CANNOT be inserted
140	    without first registering the document (the dual-write discipline D-012 relies on). The
141	    consuming model must also add ``document_fk()`` to its __table_args__ for the composite
142	    tenant-safe FK (a mixin cannot inject a multi-column FK into the host's __table_args__,
143	    exactly as TenantMixin needs the model to add tenant_fk()). UNIQUE so the registry-to-row
144	    mapping is 1:1.
145	
146	    Usage in a later module model:
147	
148	        class SalesOrder(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, DocumentMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
149	            __tablename__ = "sls_orders"
150	            __table_args__ = (tenant_unique(), tenant_fk("adm_tenants"), document_fk())
151	    """
152	
153	    @declared_attr
154	    def document_id(cls) -> Mapped[uuid.UUID]:
155	        return mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False, unique=True)
156	
157	
158	@dataclass(frozen=True)
159	class ChainNode:
160	    """One document in a flow chain — the registry projection the DocFlowViewer renders."""
161	
162	    document_id: uuid.UUID
163	    doc_type: str
164	    doc_id: uuid.UUID
165	    doc_number: str | None
166	    status: str | None
167	
168	
169	@dataclass(frozen=True)
170	class ChainEdge:
171	    """One predecessor -> successor edge in a flow chain."""
172	
173	    predecessor_document_id: uuid.UUID
174	    successor_document_id: uuid.UUID
175	    link_type: str | None
176	
177	
178	@dataclass(frozen=True)
179	class DocumentChain:
180	    """Full bidirectional flow chain around a document: every connected node plus every edge
181	    among them. Usable directly by the read API (nodes + edges for the viewer)."""
182	
183	    nodes: list[ChainNode]
184	    edges: list[ChainEdge]
185	
186	
187	async def register_document(
188	    session: AsyncSession,
189	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
190	    doc_type: str,
191	    doc_id: uuid.UUID,
192	    *,
193	    doc_number: str | None = None,
194	    status: str | None = None,
195	) -> Document:
196	    """Insert a registry row for a business document and return it (D-012). Called by the
197	    creating service in the same transaction as the business-row insert (the DocumentMixin
198	    NOT NULL FK makes skipping it a hard error). ``doc_number`` is left NULL for draft-
199	    lifecycle documents (numbered later at posting) and set for documents permanent at
200	    creation. A Core insert sets tenant_id explicitly — core/docflow is a D-007 sanctioned
201	    raw-SQL site."""
202	    document_id = uuid.uuid4()
203	    await session.execute(
204	        sa.insert(Document.__table__).values(
205	            id=document_id,
206	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
207	            doc_type=doc_type,
208	            doc_id=doc_id,
209	            doc_number=doc_number,
210	            status=status,
211	        )
212	    )
213	    return (
214	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id == document_id))
215	    ).scalar_one()
216	
217	
218	async def set_document_status(
219	    session: AsyncSession,
220	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
221	    document_id: uuid.UUID,
222	    *,
223	    status: str | None = None,
224	    doc_number: str | None = None,
225	) -> None:
226	    """Update a registry row's status and/or doc_number in the owning transaction (D-012).
227	
228	    The number is assigned at the moment a draft-lifecycle document becomes permanent (journal
229	    posting) — passing ``doc_number`` here writes it through the partial-unique (tenant,
230	    doc_number) backstop, so any numbering bug surfaces as a constraint violation. Only the
231	    provided arguments are changed (``None`` leaves the column untouched, except doc_number which
232	    is always set when supplied). A Core UPDATE addressed by (tenant_id, id) — a D-007 sanctioned
233	    explicit-tenant raw-SQL site."""
234	    values: dict[str, str | None] = {}
235	    if status is not None:
236	        values["status"] = status
237	    if doc_number is not None:
238	        values["doc_number"] = doc_number
239	    if not values:
240	        return
241	    await session.execute(
242	        sa.update(Document.__table__)
243	        .where(
244	            Document.__table__.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
245	            Document.__table__.c.id == document_id,
246	        )
247	        .values(**values)
248	    )
249	
250	
251	async def link_documents(
252	    session: AsyncSession,
253	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
254	    predecessor: uuid.UUID,
255	    successor: uuid.UUID,
256	    link_type: str | None = None,
257	) -> DocumentLink:
258	    """Create a predecessor -> successor edge and return it (D-012). The UNIQUE(tenant_id,
259	    predecessor, successor) constraint rejects a duplicate edge as an IntegrityError, and
260	    the composite tenant FKs reject endpoints from another tenant. A Core insert sets
261	    tenant_id explicitly (D-007 sanctioned site)."""
262	    link_id = uuid.uuid4()
263	    await session.execute(
264	        sa.insert(DocumentLink.__table__).values(
265	            id=link_id,
266	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
267	            predecessor_document_id=predecessor,
268	            successor_document_id=successor,
269	            link_type=link_type,
270	        )
271	    )
272	    return (
273	        await session.execute(select(DocumentLink).where(DocumentLink.id == link_id))
274	    ).scalar_one()
275	
276	
277	def _build_reachability_cte(
278	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID, start: uuid.UUID, *, forward: bool
279	) -> sa.sql.Selectable:
280	    """One recursive CTE collecting every document reachable from ``start`` in ONE direction.
281	
282	    ``forward=True`` walks successor edges (descendants), ``forward=False`` walks predecessor
283	    edges (ancestors). The recursive member carries a ``depth`` column capped at
284	    _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH and a ``path`` string of visited ids; the join excludes any node already
285	    on the path, so a diamond or cycle is traversed once and terminates (D-012 visited-path
286	    guard). Works identically on Postgres and SQLite (both support WITH RECURSIVE).
287	    """
288	    links = DocumentLink.__table__
289	    near = links.c.successor_document_id if forward else links.c.predecessor_document_id
290	    far = links.c.predecessor_document_id if forward else links.c.successor_document_id
291	
292	    # Anchor: the start node itself at depth 0. The path representation MUST match how the
293	    # recursive step casts ids (CAST(<Uuid column> AS VARCHAR)), so the start id is cast the
294	    # same way — casting a Uuid-typed literal renders dashless hex on SQLite and dashed on
295	    # PG, exactly as the column cast does, keeping the visited-path guard's LIKE comparison
296	    # apples-to-apples on both engines (a raw str(start) would carry dashes on SQLite and
297	    # silently defeat the guard).
298	    anchor = select(
299	        sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid).label("document_id"),
300	        sa.literal(0).label("depth"),
301	        sa.cast(sa.literal(start, type_=sa.Uuid), sa.String).label("path"),
302	    ).cte("reach", recursive=True)
303	
304	    # Recursive step: from each frontier node, follow edges in the chosen direction to the
305	    # node on the other end, within the tenant, skipping nodes already on the path.
306	    step = (
307	        select(
308	            far.label("document_id"),
309	            (anchor.c.depth + 1).label("depth"),
310	            (anchor.c.path + sa.literal(",") + sa.cast(far, sa.String)).label("path"),
311	        )
312	        .select_from(anchor.join(links, near == anchor.c.document_id))
313	        .where(
314	            links.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
315	            anchor.c.depth < _MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH,
316	            anchor.c.path.notlike(sa.literal("%") + sa.cast(far, sa.String) + sa.literal("%")),
317	        )
318	    )
319	    return anchor.union_all(step)
320	
321	
322	async def get_document_chain(
323	    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, document_id: uuid.UUID
324	) -> DocumentChain:
325	    """Traverse the full flow chain around ``document_id`` in BOTH directions and return its
326	    nodes + edges (D-012). Two recursive CTEs (ancestors via predecessor edges, descendants
327	    via successor edges) collect every reachable registry id; their union is the connected
328	    component containing the start node. Edges are the links whose BOTH endpoints fall in that
329	    set. Cycles and diamonds are handled by the per-CTE visited-path guard, so each node and
330	    edge appears once. Returns empty nodes/edges when the id is unknown to this tenant.
331	
332	    Tenant isolation: the CTEs filter links by tenant_id and the registry/edge reads run
333	    under the caller's tenant context (the D-007 ORM filter), so a chain query never returns
334	    another tenant's documents.
335	    """
336	    ancestors = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=False)
337	    descendants = _build_reachability_cte(tenant_id, document_id, forward=True)
338	
339	    ancestor_ids = set(
340	        (await session.execute(select(ancestors.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
341	    )
342	    descendant_ids = set(
343	        (await session.execute(select(descendants.c.document_id))).scalars().all()
344	    )
345	    reachable = ancestor_ids | descendant_ids
346	
347	    # An unknown id reaches only itself; if it is not a real registry row for this tenant,
348	    # there are no nodes to return — surface an empty chain (the router maps that to 404).
349	    document_rows = (
350	        await session.execute(select(Document).where(Document.id.in_(reachable)))
351	    ).scalars().all()
352	    if not document_rows:
353	        return DocumentChain(nodes=[], edges=[])
354	
355	    present_ids = {row.id for row in document_rows}
356	    nodes = [
357	        ChainNode(
358	            document_id=row.id,
359	            doc_type=row.doc_type,
360	            doc_id=row.doc_id,
361	            doc_number=row.doc_number,
362	            status=row.status,
363	        )
364	        for row in document_rows
365	    ]
366	
367	    link_rows = (
368	        await session.execute(
369	            select(DocumentLink).where(
370	                DocumentLink.predecessor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
371	                DocumentLink.successor_document_id.in_(present_ids),
372	            )
373	        )
374	    ).scalars().all()
375	    edges = [
376	        ChainEdge(
377	            predecessor_document_id=link.predecessor_document_id,
378	            successor_document_id=link.successor_document_id,
379	            link_type=link.link_type,
380	        )
381	        for link in link_rows
382	    ]
383	
384	    return DocumentChain(nodes=nodes, edges=edges)

1	"""The universal journal: header + lines (D-017), the heart of Atlas finance.
2	
3	One append-only line table is the single source of truth for every FI/CO view (D-021); the
4	header carries entry-level lifecycle and the lines carry the postings plus every dimension a
5	statement projects from. Denormalized ``is_posted``/``posting_date``/``fiscal_period_id`` on the
6	line (set during the two-flush posting protocol) let projections query lines with NO header join
7	(D-021), which is why those columns live on the line at all.
8	
9	Money columns use ``MoneyType`` (D-015): exact NUMERIC on Postgres, INTEGER micro-units on
10	SQLite, so the balance trigger's SUM and the one-side CHECK are exact on both engines. For v1,
11	functional amounts EQUAL transaction amounts (single functional currency, posting-time FX
12	translation lands in 4.3) — the columns exist now so the schema and triggers are FX-ready.
13	
14	Constraints declared here (rendered by migration 0009):
15	- ``ck_fin_journal_lines_one_side``: exactly one of debit/credit positive per line, the other
16	  zero — written on the stored columns so it holds on PG NUMERIC and SQLite micro-unit ints.
17	- the per-dialect TRIGGERS (period-open, balance, header immutability, line immutability) are
18	  NOT model constraints; they are hand-written DDL in the migration (D-017/D-018/D-022).
19	
20	Dimension columns (cost_center_id, profit_center_id, project_id, item_id, partner_id) are plain
21	``sa.Uuid`` WITHOUT FKs for now: the CO/project/inventory masters land in later PLAN phases
22	(4.7 controlling, 5 inventory, 11 projects); the ids are stored on the line today and FK'd when
23	those parent tables exist. partner_type + partner_id carry AP/AR open-item linkage (4.4+).
24	"""
25	
26	import uuid
27	from datetime import date, datetime
28	
29	import sqlalchemy as sa
30	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
31	
32	from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
33	from app.core.models import (
34	    AuditMixin,
35	    Base,
36	    TenantMixin,
37	    TimestampMixin,
38	    UuidPKMixin,
39	    tenant_fk,
40	    tenant_unique,
41	)
42	from app.core.money import MoneyType
43	from app.modules.finance.constants import DocumentType, EntryStatus
44	
45	# Bare CHECK token (the D-022 ck convention wraps it as ck_<table>_<name>). Compares the STORED
46	# representation (NUMERIC on PG, micro-unit INTEGER on SQLite) so "> 0" / "= 0" hold on both.
47	_ONE_SIDE_CHECK = (
48	    "(transaction_debit_amount > 0 AND transaction_credit_amount = 0) "
49	    "OR (transaction_credit_amount > 0 AND transaction_debit_amount = 0)"
50	)
51	
52	
53	class JournalEntry(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
54	    """A journal-entry header (D-017). Registered in core_documents at creation (DocumentMixin)
55	    with doc_number NULL; the gapless ``entry_number`` is claimed at POSTING (D-012), so an
56	    abandoned draft burns no number — hence ``entry_number`` is NULLABLE with a partial unique
57	    index. An entry is single-transaction-currency (cross-currency events become multiple
58	    entries). ``reverses_entry_id`` points at the original an entry reverses;
59	    ``reversed_by_entry_id`` points at the reversing entry — both self composite tenant FKs.
60	    Audited (D-010): every financial mutation is auditable."""
61	
62	    __tablename__ = "fin_journal_entries"
63	    __table_args__ = (
64	        tenant_unique(),
65	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
66	        document_fk(),
67	        # Self composite tenant FKs: a reversal linkage can never cross tenants. Distinct
68	        # explicit names (the D-022 column-0 convention would collide on two self-FKs).
69	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
70	            ["tenant_id", "reverses_entry_id"],
71	            ["fin_journal_entries.tenant_id", "fin_journal_entries.id"],
72	            name="fk_fin_journal_entries_reverses_entry_id_fin_journal_entries",
73	        ),
74	        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
75	            ["tenant_id", "reversed_by_entry_id"],
76	            ["fin_journal_entries.tenant_id", "fin_journal_entries.id"],
77	            name="fk_fin_journal_entries_reversed_by_entry_id_fin_journal_entries",
78	        ),
79	        # Composite tenant FK: the resolved period belongs to the same tenant.
80	        tenant_fk("fin_fiscal_periods", "fiscal_period_id"),
81	        # The gapless-number partial unique index is declared after the class (it needs the
82	        # column object for its dialect partial predicate, expressed without raw SQL so the
83	        # app/modules grep gate stays satisfied — see below).
84	    )
85	
86	    # NULL until posting (D-012 claim-at-permanence); the partial unique index above backstops it.
87	    entry_number: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=True)
88	    posting_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
89	    # Resolved from posting_date at posting (D-018); nullable until then. The DB period trigger
90	    # re-derives by date so a wrong fiscal_period_id can never smuggle a posting into a closed
91	    # period.
92	    fiscal_period_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
93	    document_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
94	        sa.String(20), nullable=False, default=DocumentType.JOURNAL.value, server_default="JOURNAL"
95	    )
96	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
97	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
98	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
99	        sa.String(10), nullable=False, default=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value, server_default="DRAFT"
100	    )
101	    reverses_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
102	    reversed_by_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
103	    posted_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True)
104	
105	
106	class JournalLine(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
107	    """A journal line (D-017): one posting on one account, one-sided (debit XOR credit). NOT
108	    AuditMixin — lines are written once with their immutable entry and never mutated after the
109	    posting flush, and the header's audit row records the entry-level change; auditing every
110	    line would double the trail with no extra signal (documented exclusion). The denormalized
111	    ``is_posted``/``posting_date``/``fiscal_period_id`` are set during the DRAFT->POSTED flush so
112	    statement projections read lines with no header join (D-021)."""
113	
114	    __tablename__ = "fin_journal_lines"
115	    __table_args__ = (
116	        sa.UniqueConstraint(
117	            "tenant_id",
118	            "journal_entry_id",
119	            "line_number",
120	            name="uq_fin_journal_lines_tenant_id_journal_entry_id_line_number",
121	        ),
122	        tenant_unique(),
123	        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
124	        tenant_fk("fin_journal_entries", "journal_entry_id"),
125	        tenant_fk("fin_accounts", "account_id"),
126	        sa.CheckConstraint(_ONE_SIDE_CHECK, name="one_side"),
127	        # The statement-projection partial index is declared after the class (see below).
128	    )
129	
130	    journal_entry_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
131	    line_number: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=False)
132	    account_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
133	    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
134	
135	    # Transaction-currency amounts (the entry's currency). Exactly one side is > 0 (one-side
136	    # CHECK). MoneyType: exact on both engines so the balance trigger's SUM is exact.
137	    transaction_debit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
138	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
139	    )
140	    transaction_credit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
141	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
142	    )
143	    # Functional-currency amounts. v1: equal to the transaction amounts (single functional
144	    # currency; posting-time FX translation in 4.3). The balance trigger SUM-checks THESE.
145	    functional_debit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
146	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
147	    )
148	    functional_credit_amount: Mapped[object] = mapped_column(
149	        MoneyType(), nullable=False, default=0, server_default="0"
150	    )
151	    currency_code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(3), nullable=False)
152	
153	    # Dimensions (all nullable; no FK yet — masters land in later phases, see module docstring).
154	    cost_center_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
155	    profit_center_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
156	    project_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
157	    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
158	    # AP/AR open-item linkage (4.4+): partner_type ('VENDOR'|'CUSTOMER') + partner_id.
159	    partner_type: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(20), nullable=True)
160	    partner_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
161	
162	    # Denormalized for statement projection (D-021): set during the posting transaction so a
163	    # projection queries lines with no header join.
164	    is_posted: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
165	        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
166	    )
167	    posting_date: Mapped[date | None] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=True)
168	    fiscal_period_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
169	
170	
171	# Partial indexes declared OUTSIDE the class bodies so their dialect predicate is a column
172	# expression (``.isnot(None)`` / the boolean column) rather than a raw SQL string literal — the
173	# D-007 grep gate bans raw-SQL constructs under app/modules/. Both dialect kwargs are required
174	# (each engine needs its own partial-index predicate, D-012/D-021); the migration renders the same.
175	
176	# Gapless numbers: many drafts may have NULL entry_number, never two the SAME (D-012).
177	sa.Index(
178	    "uq_fin_journal_entries_tenant_id_entry_number",
179	    JournalEntry.tenant_id,
180	    JournalEntry.entry_number,
181	    unique=True,
182	    postgresql_where=JournalEntry.entry_number.isnot(None),
183	    sqlite_where=JournalEntry.entry_number.isnot(None),
184	)
185	
186	# Statement-projection covering index (D-021): lines grouped by account over a date range, only
187	# the posted ones. Both dialect partial predicates (each engine needs its own); on Postgres the
188	# two functional amount columns are INCLUDE'd so the statement aggregate is an index-only scan
189	# (the kwarg is harmlessly ignored on SQLite). Migration 0015 brings the physical index up to this
190	# covering shape — 0009 created the bare partial index; this declaration is its final form.
191	sa.Index(
192	    "ix_fin_journal_lines_proj",
193	    JournalLine.tenant_id,
194	    JournalLine.account_id,
195	    JournalLine.posting_date,
196	    postgresql_where=JournalLine.is_posted,
197	    sqlite_where=JournalLine.is_posted,
198	    postgresql_include=["functional_debit_amount", "functional_credit_amount"],
199	)
