1	"""The universal-journal posting engine (D-017): draft creation, two-flush posting, reversal.
2	
3	Every invariant lives at BOTH the service (here, for a clean 422) and the DB (migration 0009
4	triggers, the bypass-proof backstop). Three load-bearing mechanisms (D-017): (1) TWO-FLUSH
5	posting — the uow does not guarantee cross-table UPDATE order, so we flush the loaded lines'
6	``is_posted`` while the entry is still DRAFT (the line trigger keys on OLD.is_posted=FALSE),
7	THEN flush the header POSTED (balance + period triggers fire there); (2) LOADED-object mutation,
8	never bulk ``update()``, so audit diffs are captured and the audit bulk-write assertion holds
9	(D-010); (3) REVERSAL-only correction — a posted entry is never edited/deleted, only reversed.
10	
11	For v1 functional amounts EQUAL transaction amounts (single functional currency; FX in 4.3). The
12	balance check sums functional amounts, exact on both engines (MoneyType stores NUMERIC / micro-unit
13	ints, D-015).
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	import uuid
19	from datetime import UTC, date, datetime
20	from decimal import Decimal
21	
22	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
23	
24	from app.core import docflow
25	from app.core.events import publish
26	from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, ValidationFailedError
27	from app.core.numbering import claim_number, ensure_sequence
28	from app.modules.finance import queries
29	from app.modules.finance.constants import (
30	    JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
31	    JOURNAL_NUMBER_PADDING,
32	    JOURNAL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
33	    JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
34	    DocumentType,
35	    EntryStatus,
36	    PeriodStatus,
37	)
38	from app.modules.finance.events import JournalEntryPosted, JournalEntryReversed
39	from app.modules.finance.models import JournalEntry, JournalLine
40	from app.modules.finance.schemas import JournalEntryCreate
41	from app.modules.finance.service.fx_translation import translate_entry_lines
42	from app.modules.finance.service.journal_read import (
43	    entry_totals,
44	    get_entry,
45	    load_lines,
46	)
47	from app.modules.finance.service.journal_validate import (
48	    assert_line_one_sided,
49	    require_dimensions,
50	    require_postable_accounts,
51	)
52	
53	# core/docflow link type for the reverses-edge (D-012 vocabulary).
54	_REVERSES_LINK = "reverses"
55	
56	
57	async def create_draft_entry(
58	    session: AsyncSession,
59	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
60	    payload: JournalEntryCreate,
61	    *,
62	    functional_amounts: list[tuple[Decimal, Decimal]] | None = None,
63	) -> JournalEntry:
64	    """Create a DRAFT entry + lines (D-017). Validates: >= 2 lines, each one-sided, all accounts
65	    exist + postable + same tenant, and any cost-/profit-centre dimension exists in the tenant
66	    (PLAN 4.7, the service-level integrity replacing the absent FK on the trigger-bearing
67	    journal-lines table per D-022). Registers the document (no number; claimed at posting, D-012).
68	    Does NOT claim a number / resolve the period — both at posting.
69	
70	    Default: functional == transaction, balanced in TRANSACTION terms (the posting protocol then
71	    translates FX). With explicit ``functional_amounts`` ((debit, credit) per line; AP/AR clearing,
72	    D-019) those become the functional amounts and the balance check is on the FUNCTIONAL sums — a
73	    mixed-currency clearing entry balances only in functional, posted with skip_translation."""
74	    if len(payload.lines) < 2:
75	        raise ValidationFailedError(
76	            message="A journal entry needs at least two lines",
77	            code="finance.journal_too_few_lines",
78	        )
79	
80	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
81	        assert_line_one_sided(line, index)
82	    # Balance on transaction sides by default, on explicit functional sides for a (mixed-currency)
83	    # clearing entry where only functional must balance.
84	    sides = functional_amounts or [
85	        (ln.transaction_debit_amount, ln.transaction_credit_amount) for ln in payload.lines
86	    ]
87	    total_debit = sum((d for d, _c in sides), Decimal(0))
88	    total_credit = sum((c for _d, c in sides), Decimal(0))
89	    if total_debit != total_credit:
90	        raise ValidationFailedError(
91	            message="Journal entry debits and credits must balance",
92	            code="finance.journal_unbalanced",
93	            details={"total_debit": str(total_debit), "total_credit": str(total_credit)},
94	        )
95	
96	    account_ids = {line.account_id for line in payload.lines}
97	    await require_postable_accounts(session, tenant_id, account_ids)
98	    await require_dimensions(session, tenant_id, payload)
99	    entry_id = uuid.uuid4()
100	    document = await docflow.register_document(
101	        session,
102	        tenant_id,
103	        JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
104	        entry_id,
105	        doc_number=None,
106	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
107	    )
108	    entry = JournalEntry(
109	        id=entry_id,
110	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
111	        document_id=document.id,
112	        posting_date=payload.posting_date,
113	        currency_code=payload.currency_code,
114	        description=payload.description,
115	        document_type=DocumentType(payload.document_type).value,
116	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
117	    )
118	    session.add(entry)
119	    for index, line in enumerate(payload.lines, start=1):
120	        # ``sides`` is functional == transaction by default (posting translates FX), or the explicit
121	        # clearing functional amounts when supplied — either way one (debit, credit) per line.
122	        func_debit, func_credit = sides[index - 1]
123	        session.add(
124	            JournalLine(
125	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
126	                journal_entry_id=entry_id,
127	                line_number=index,
128	                account_id=line.account_id,
129	                description=line.description,
130	                transaction_debit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
131	                transaction_credit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
132	                functional_debit_amount=func_debit,
133	                functional_credit_amount=func_credit,
134	                currency_code=payload.currency_code,
135	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
136	                profit_center_id=line.profit_center_id,
137	                project_id=line.project_id,
138	                item_id=line.item_id,
139	                partner_type=line.partner_type,
140	                partner_id=line.partner_id,
141	            )
142	        )
143	    await session.flush()
144	    return entry
145	
146	
147	async def post_entry(
148	    session: AsyncSession,
149	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
150	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
151	    *,
152	    rate_override: Decimal | None = None,
153	    skip_translation: bool = False,
154	) -> JournalEntry:
155	    """THE posting protocol (D-017 two-flush). Validates DRAFT + balanced, resolves + checks the
156	    open period from posting_date (422 before touching the DB), translates foreign-currency
157	    functional amounts (D-019; an explicit ``rate_override`` wins over the looked-up SPOT rate),
158	    claims the gapless number in this transaction, then flushes the loaded lines (still DRAFT) and
159	    finally the POSTED header (balance + period triggers fire there). Publishes JournalEntryPosted;
160	
161	    ``skip_translation`` (D-019, used by AP/AR clearing): the caller has ALREADY set each line's
162	    functional amounts (e.g. a payment clears its open items at the bill's frozen rate while the
163	    bank is at the payment rate, with a realized-FX line absorbing the difference). The engine then
164	    only validates those pre-computed functional amounts balance, never re-rating them — the one
165	    case where functional != transaction × a single entry rate.
166	    the caller commits via uow."""
167	    entry = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
168	    if entry.status != EntryStatus.DRAFT.value:
169	        raise ConflictError(
170	            message="Only a draft journal entry can be posted",
171	            code="finance.journal_not_draft",
172	            details={"status": entry.status},
173	        )
174	
175	    lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
176	    if len(lines) < 2:
177	        raise ValidationFailedError(
178	            message="A journal entry needs at least two lines",
179	            code="finance.journal_too_few_lines",
180	        )
181	
182	    # FX translation (D-019): recompute functional amounts at the posting rate when the entry is in
183	    # a foreign currency, balancing the functional residual into the largest line. After this the
184	    # functional sums (which the balance trigger checks) are exact and equal. Skipped when the
185	    # caller pre-computed functional amounts (AP/AR clearing realized FX) — the balance check below
186	    # then validates those.
187	    if not skip_translation:
188	        await translate_entry_lines(session, tenant_id, entry, lines, rate_override)
189	
190	    debit, credit = entry_totals(lines)
191	    if debit != credit or debit <= 0:
192	        raise ValidationFailedError(
193	            message="Journal entry debits and credits must balance and be positive",
194	            code="finance.journal_unbalanced",
195	            details={"total_debit": str(debit), "total_credit": str(credit)},
196	        )
197	
198	    # Period resolution + open check FIRST (service-level half of D-018); the trigger backstops.
199	    period = await queries.find_period_for_date(session, tenant_id, entry.posting_date)
200	    if period is None or period.status != PeriodStatus.OPEN.value:
201	        raise ValidationFailedError(
202	            message="The posting date is not within an open fiscal period",
203	            code="finance.period_closed",
204	            details={"posting_date": entry.posting_date.isoformat()},
205	        )
206	
207	    # Claim the gapless number in this transaction (D-012): gapless because the claim and the
208	    # POSTED commit succeed or roll back together.
209	    await ensure_sequence(
210	        session,
211	        tenant_id,
212	        JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME,
213	        JOURNAL_NUMBER_PREFIX,
214	        JOURNAL_NUMBER_PADDING,
215	        year_reset=True,
216	    )
217	    entry_number = await claim_number(
218	        session, tenant_id, JOURNAL_SEQUENCE_NAME, on_date=entry.posting_date
219	    )
220	
221	    # Flush 1: denormalize onto the loaded lines while the entry is still DRAFT.
222	    for line in lines:
223	        line.is_posted = True
224	        line.posting_date = entry.posting_date
225	        line.fiscal_period_id = period.id
226	    await session.flush()
227	
228	    # Flush 2: promote the header. The period + balance triggers fire on this DRAFT->POSTED UPDATE.
229	    entry.entry_number = entry_number
230	    entry.fiscal_period_id = period.id
231	    entry.status = EntryStatus.POSTED.value
232	    entry.posted_at = datetime.now(UTC)
233	    await session.flush()
234	
235	    await docflow.set_document_status(
236	        session,
237	        tenant_id,
238	        entry.document_id,
239	        status=EntryStatus.POSTED.value,
240	        doc_number=entry_number,
241	    )
242	
243	    publish(
244	        session,
245	        JournalEntryPosted(
246	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
247	            entry_id=entry.id,
248	            entry_number=entry_number,
249	            document_type=entry.document_type,
250	            posting_date=entry.posting_date.isoformat(),
251	            currency_code=entry.currency_code,
252	            total_functional_amount=debit,
253	            account_ids=tuple(line.account_id for line in lines),
254	        ),
255	    )
256	    return entry
257	
258	
259	async def reverse_entry(
260	    session: AsyncSession,
261	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
262	    entry_id: uuid.UUID,
263	    reversal_date: date,
264	    description: str | None = None,
265	) -> JournalEntry:
266	    """Reverse a POSTED entry (D-017). Creates a NEW same-document_type entry with each line's
267	    debit/credit SWAPPED, posts it into ``reversal_date``'s open period (its own number), then
268	    sets the original REVERSED + reversed_by_entry_id — the ONLY mutation the immutability trigger
269	    permits. Links the two documents ('reverses'), publishes JournalEntryReversed, returns the
270	    reversing entry."""
271	    original = await get_entry(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
272	    if original.status != EntryStatus.POSTED.value:
273	        raise ConflictError(
274	            message="Only a posted journal entry can be reversed",
275	            code="finance.journal_not_posted",
276	            details={"status": original.status},
277	        )
278	    if original.reversed_by_entry_id is not None:
279	        raise ConflictError(
280	            message="This journal entry has already been reversed",
281	            code="finance.journal_already_reversed",
282	        )
283	
284	    original_lines = await load_lines(session, tenant_id, entry_id)
285	
286	    reversal_id = uuid.uuid4()
287	    reversal_document = await docflow.register_document(
288	        session,
289	        tenant_id,
290	        JOURNAL_ENTRY_DOC_TYPE,
291	        reversal_id,
292	        doc_number=None,
293	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
294	    )
295	    reversal = JournalEntry(
296	        id=reversal_id,
297	        tenant_id=tenant_id,
298	        document_id=reversal_document.id,
299	        posting_date=reversal_date,
300	        currency_code=original.currency_code,
301	        description=description
302	        or f"Reversal of {original.entry_number or original.id}",
303	        document_type=original.document_type,
304	        status=EntryStatus.DRAFT.value,
305	        reverses_entry_id=original.id,
306	    )
307	    session.add(reversal)
308	    for line in original_lines:
309	        session.add(
310	            JournalLine(
311	                tenant_id=tenant_id,
312	                journal_entry_id=reversal_id,
313	                line_number=line.line_number,
314	                account_id=line.account_id,
315	                description=line.description,
316	                # Swap debit <-> credit in both currency pairs (frozen functional amounts).
317	                transaction_debit_amount=line.transaction_credit_amount,
318	                transaction_credit_amount=line.transaction_debit_amount,
319	                functional_debit_amount=line.functional_credit_amount,
320	                functional_credit_amount=line.functional_debit_amount,
321	                currency_code=line.currency_code,
322	                cost_center_id=line.cost_center_id,
323	                profit_center_id=line.profit_center_id,
324	                project_id=line.project_id,
325	                item_id=line.item_id,
326	                partner_type=line.partner_type,
327	                partner_id=line.partner_id,
328	            )
329	        )
330	    await session.flush()
331	
332	    # Post the reversing entry (claims its own number, runs the same period/balance checks).
333	    await post_entry(session, tenant_id, reversal_id)
334	
335	    # The single sanctioned mutation on a POSTED original (immutability trigger permits exactly
336	    # this: status POSTED->REVERSED with reversed_by_entry_id set).
337	    original.reversed_by_entry_id = reversal_id
338	    original.status = EntryStatus.REVERSED.value
339	    await session.flush()
340	
341	    await docflow.set_document_status(
342	        session, tenant_id, original.document_id, status=EntryStatus.REVERSED.value
343	    )
344	    await docflow.link_documents(
345	        session,
346	        tenant_id,
347	        predecessor=original.document_id,
348	        successor=reversal.document_id,
349	        link_type=_REVERSES_LINK,
350	    )
351	
352	    await session.refresh(reversal)
353	    publish(
354	        session,
355	        JournalEntryReversed(
356	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
357	            entry_id=original.id,
358	            reversal_entry_id=reversal.id,
359	            reversal_entry_number=reversal.entry_number or "",
360	            document_type=original.document_type,
361	            reversal_date=reversal_date.isoformat(),
362	        ),
363	    )
364	    return reversal

1	"""D-013 idempotency keys: reservation + atomic completion via route capture.
2	
3	The mechanism, exactly as D-013 prescribes, in two phases:
4	
5	* **Phase 1 (reserve).** ``Idempotent("endpoint")`` reads the ``Idempotency-Key`` header,
6	  hashes the canonical request body, and calls :func:`reserve`, which opens a SEPARATE
7	  short-lived session, INSERTs an ``IN_PROGRESS`` row, and COMMITs immediately. Two concurrent
8	  duplicates therefore collide on the natural composite PK ``(tenant_id, endpoint, key)`` — PG's
9	  unique index arbitrates, SQLite's single-writer lock serializes. On collision the existing row
10	  decides the outcome: ``COMPLETED`` + matching hash → REPLAY the stored response verbatim with
11	  header ``Idempotency-Replayed: true`` and no business logic; ``COMPLETED`` + different hash →
12	  422 ``idempotency.key_reuse`` (a client bug reusing a key for a different body); ``IN_PROGRESS``
13	  → 409 ``idempotency.in_progress`` (a concurrent duplicate is still running).
14	
15	* **Phase 2 (capture).** The dependency YIELDS an :class:`IdempotencyContext` bound to the
16	  request's BUSINESS session. The handler's last act is ``idem.capture(read_schema)`` — it
17	  ``model_dump``s the exact schema FastAPI will serialize and STAGES the completion UPDATE
18	  (status → COMPLETED, response_status, response_body, completed_at) on the business session, so
19	  the document and the replay record commit ATOMICALLY in one ``run_in_uow`` transaction. The
20	  cardinal invariant: a replayable response exists iff the document exists.
21	
22	* **Fail-closed.** On a BUSINESS EXCEPTION, the dependency's teardown deletes the dangling
23	  IN_PROGRESS reservation (committed in its own session) so the client may retry the same key, and
24	  re-raises — the app's exception handlers render the proper error envelope. (Atlas commits the
25	  business work via ``run_in_uow`` INSIDE the handler, so a failed handler has already rolled the
26	  document AND the staged capture UPDATE back; only the separately-committed reservation needs
27	  cleanup.) On a FORGOTTEN ``capture()`` (handler returned 2xx but never captured), the teardown
28	  deletes the dangling reservation and logs a server error; it cannot convert the already-sent 2xx
29	  to a 500 because the run_in_uow commit precedes teardown — a documented deviation from D-013's
30	  literal "teardown rolls back", which assumed a deferred session-dependency commit (DECISIONS.md).
31	
32	Replay short-circuit mechanism (FastAPI-idiomatic): :func:`reserve` raises
33	:class:`IdempotencyReplay` carrying the stored response. ``IdempotencyReplay`` is an
34	``AtlasError`` subtype whose dedicated handler in ``app.main`` writes the stored
35	status+body+header — so a completed-key replay never reaches the handler body and the side
36	effect cannot run twice. A first-time request instead yields the context normally.
37	"""
38	
39	import hashlib
40	import logging
41	import uuid
42	from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
43	from dataclasses import dataclass
44	from datetime import UTC, datetime
45	from typing import Annotated, Any
46	
47	import sqlalchemy as sa
48	from fastapi import Depends, Header, Request
49	from sqlalchemy import select
50	from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
51	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker
52	from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
53	
54	from app.core.audit import json_safe
55	from app.core.db import get_session, get_session_factory
56	from app.core.exceptions import AtlasError, ConflictError, ValidationFailedError
57	from app.core.models import JSON_VARIANT, Base, TenantMixin, tenant_fk
58	from app.core.tenancy import get_current_tenant_id, system_context
59	
60	# This module imports core/db (for the get_session / get_session_factory dependencies the
61	# Idempotent guard composes), so unlike numbering.py / docflow.py it is registered on
62	# Base.metadata from the BOTTOM of core/db.py — AFTER db, audit and tenancy finish loading —
63	# rather than via core/models' trailing import, which would run mid-cycle and dead-lock on the
64	# db -> audit -> models chain. The registration site is documented there.
65	
66	logger = logging.getLogger("atlas")
67	
68	STATUS_IN_PROGRESS = "in_progress"
69	STATUS_COMPLETED = "completed"
70	
71	# Header marking a replayed response (D-013): clients can tell a fresh execution from a replay.
72	REPLAYED_HEADER = "Idempotency-Replayed"
73	
74	
75	class IdempotencyKey(TenantMixin, Base):
76	    """Reservation row (D-013). The PRIMARY KEY is the NATURAL composite
77	    ``(tenant_id, endpoint, key)`` exactly as D-013 prescribes — deliberately NOT UuidPKMixin:
78	    the composite key IS the collision point that serializes concurrent duplicates, so a surrogate
79	    id plus a UNIQUE would be redundant indirection. TenantMixin still applies (the row is
80	    tenant-scoped and the D-007 filter/stamp run on it); tenant_id participates in the PK so the
81	    composite is already tenant-unique. Not AuditMixin: reservation rows are request-control
82	    infrastructure, not business state (auditing them would be noise — documented exclusion)."""
83	
84	    __tablename__ = "core_idempotency_keys"
85	    __table_args__ = (tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),)
86	
87	    # Override TenantMixin's tenant_id to make it part of the composite PK (the mixin declares it
88	    # non-PK). All three PK members carry primary_key=True so the mapper's PK matches the
89	    # migration's PrimaryKeyConstraint(tenant_id, endpoint, key) — the natural key D-013 mandates.
90	    # index=True preserves the mixin's standalone tenant_id index (the D-007 mapper-enumeration
91	    # invariant requires every tenant-scoped table to carry one, uniform across the schema even
92	    # though the composite PK already leads with tenant_id).
93	    tenant_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, primary_key=True, index=True)
94	    endpoint: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), primary_key=True)
95	    key: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), primary_key=True)
96	    status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(20), nullable=False)
97	    request_hash: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(64), nullable=False)
98	    response_status: Mapped[int | None] = mapped_column(sa.Integer, nullable=True)
99	    response_body: Mapped[Any] = mapped_column(JSON_VARIANT, nullable=True)
100	    created_at: Mapped[datetime] = mapped_column(
101	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False, server_default=sa.func.now()
102	    )
103	    completed_at: Mapped[datetime | None] = mapped_column(
104	        sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=True
105	    )
106	
107	
108	def compute_request_hash(body: bytes) -> str:
109	    """sha256 hex of the raw request body (D-013). The raw bytes are the canonical form here:
110	    a replay must present the byte-identical body, and hashing bytes avoids re-serialization
111	    ambiguity. An empty body hashes to the sha256 of b'' — stable and well-defined."""
112	    return hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest()
113	
114	
115	class IdempotencyReplay(AtlasError):
116	    """Raised by reserve() when a COMPLETED key with a matching hash is replayed. NOT an error
117	    in the user sense — its dedicated handler in app.main writes the stored response verbatim
118	    (status + body + Idempotency-Replayed header), short-circuiting the route so the side effect
119	    never runs twice. status_code/details carry the stored response across to the handler."""
120	
121	    def __init__(self, response_status: int, response_body: Any) -> None:
122	        super().__init__(
123	            code="idempotency.replayed",
124	            message="Replaying a previously completed idempotent response",
125	            status_code=response_status,
126	        )
127	        self.response_body = response_body
128	
129	
130	@dataclass
131	class IdempotencyContext:
132	    """Yielded to the handler (Phase 2). ``capture`` stages the completion UPDATE on the BUSINESS
133	    session so document + replay record commit atomically; ``captured`` lets the teardown detect a
134	    forgotten capture (fail-closed). ``factory`` + identity are kept so the teardown can run the
135	    separate-session cleanup that deletes the reservation on a forgotten-capture or business
136	    failure."""
137	
138	    session: AsyncSession
139	    factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]
140	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
141	    endpoint: str
142	    key: str
143	    captured: bool = False
144	
145	    async def capture[T](self, response: T, *, status_code: int = 200) -> T:
146	        """Write ``UPDATE ... SET status='completed', response_status, response_body,
147	        completed_at=now()`` on the BUSINESS session (no commit) and return ``response``
148	        UNCHANGED. Call it INSIDE the ``run_in_uow`` work, right after the document is created::
149	
150	            async def work() -> None:
151	                doc = create_document(...)
152	                await session.flush()
153	                holder['read'] = await idem.capture(DocRead.model_validate(doc))
154	            await run_in_uow(session, work)
155	            return holder['read']
156	
157	        The UPDATE joins the request's open transaction, so ``run_in_uow``'s single commit persists
158	        the document AND this replay record atomically — they commit or roll back together
159	        (D-013's cardinal invariant: a replayable response exists iff the document exists). The
160	        body is serialized to the exact JSON FastAPI will emit, so a future replay reproduces it
161	        verbatim.
162	
163	        A Core UPDATE under system_context: the reservation is addressed by its full composite PK,
164	        so no tenant filter is needed and bypassing the ORM stamp keeps it a pure data write."""
165	        body = _serialize_response(response)
166	        with system_context():
167	            await self.session.execute(
168	                sa.update(IdempotencyKey.__table__)
169	                .where(
170	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.tenant_id == self.tenant_id,
171	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.endpoint == self.endpoint,
172	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.key == self.key,
173	                )
174	                .values(
175	                    status=STATUS_COMPLETED,
176	                    response_status=status_code,
177	                    response_body=body,
178	                    completed_at=datetime.now(UTC),
179	                )
180	            )
181	        self.captured = True
182	        return response
183	
184	
185	def _serialize_response(response: Any) -> Any:
186	    """Coerce a route's return value (a Pydantic model, a dict, or a primitive) to the
187	    JSON-safe form FastAPI would serialize, so a replay reproduces it byte-for-byte."""
188	    if hasattr(response, "model_dump"):
189	        return response.model_dump(mode="json")
190	    return json_safe(response)
191	
192	
193	async def reserve(
194	    factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession],
195	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
196	    endpoint: str,
197	    key: str,
198	    request_hash: str,
199	) -> None:
200	    """Phase 1 (D-013). Open a SEPARATE session, INSERT the IN_PROGRESS reservation, and COMMIT
201	    immediately so two concurrent duplicates collide on the composite PK. On collision, load the
202	    existing row and decide: replay (raise IdempotencyReplay), key-reuse (422), or in-progress
203	    (409). Runs under system_context so the explicit-tenant_id insert/select bypass ORM stamping
204	    on this out-of-band session; the composite-FK backstop still rejects a bogus tenant_id."""
205	    async with factory() as session:
206	        try:
207	            with system_context():
208	                await session.execute(
209	                    sa.insert(IdempotencyKey.__table__).values(
210	                        tenant_id=tenant_id,
211	                        endpoint=endpoint,
212	                        key=key,
213	                        status=STATUS_IN_PROGRESS,
214	                        request_hash=request_hash,
215	                    )
216	                )
217	                await session.commit()
218	            return
219	        except IntegrityError:
220	            await session.rollback()
221	
222	        # Collision: a row already exists for (tenant, endpoint, key). Load and arbitrate.
223	        with system_context():
224	            existing = (
225	                await session.execute(
226	                    select(IdempotencyKey).where(
227	                        IdempotencyKey.tenant_id == tenant_id,
228	                        IdempotencyKey.endpoint == endpoint,
229	                        IdempotencyKey.key == key,
230	                    )
231	                )
232	            ).scalar_one()
233	
234	    if existing.status == STATUS_COMPLETED:
235	        if existing.request_hash == request_hash:
236	            raise IdempotencyReplay(existing.response_status or 200, existing.response_body)
237	        raise ValidationFailedError(
238	            message="Idempotency-Key was reused with a different request body",
239	            code="idempotency.key_reuse",
240	        )
241	    # IN_PROGRESS: a concurrent duplicate is still running its business work.
242	    raise ConflictError(
243	        message="A request with this Idempotency-Key is already in progress",
244	        code="idempotency.in_progress",
245	    )
246	
247	
248	async def _cleanup_reservation(
249	    factory: async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession],
250	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
251	    endpoint: str,
252	    key: str,
253	) -> None:
254	    """Delete an IN_PROGRESS reservation in its OWN committed session (D-013 fail-closed). Run
255	    when the handler failed or forgot to capture, so the client may retry the same key. Only
256	    deletes while status is still IN_PROGRESS — never removes a COMPLETED replay record."""
257	    async with factory() as session:
258	        with system_context():
259	            await session.execute(
260	                sa.delete(IdempotencyKey.__table__).where(
261	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
262	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.endpoint == endpoint,
263	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.key == key,
264	                    IdempotencyKey.__table__.c.status == STATUS_IN_PROGRESS,
265	                )
266	            )
267	            await session.commit()
268	
269	
270	class Idempotent:
271	    """FastAPI dependency factory (D-013). A guarded route declares it AFTER the principal
272	    dependency (so the D-007 tenant context is set when reserve runs) and captures inside the uow::
273	
274	        @router.post("/journal-entries/{id}/post")
275	        async def post_journal(
276	            current: CurrentUserDep,
277	            session: SessionDep,
278	            idem: IdempotentDep = Depends(Idempotent("finance.journal.post")),
279	        ):
280	            holder = {}
281	            async def work() -> None:
282	                entry = await post_entry(session, ...)        # create the document
283	                holder['read'] = await idem.capture(JournalEntryRead.model_validate(entry))
284	            await run_in_uow(session, work)                   # commits document + replay record
285	            return holder['read']
286	
287	    The ``endpoint`` string is the stable D-013 route identifier (METHOD + template, or a chosen
288	    key) that scopes reservations per endpoint, so one client UUID per form submission is safe."""
289	
290	    def __init__(self, endpoint: str) -> None:
291	        self.endpoint = endpoint
292	
293	    async def __call__(
294	        self,
295	        request: Request,
296	        session: Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)],
297	        factory: Annotated[async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], Depends(get_session_factory)],
298	        idempotency_key: Annotated[str | None, Header(alias="Idempotency-Key")] = None,
299	    ) -> AsyncIterator[IdempotencyContext]:
300	        if not idempotency_key:
301	            raise ValidationFailedError(
302	                message="The Idempotency-Key header is required for this endpoint",
303	                code="idempotency.key_required",
304	            )
305	        # tenant_id from the D-007 ContextVar that get_current_user set. A guarded route declares
306	        # the principal dependency BEFORE this one (the codebase convention: every router lists
307	        # ``current: CurrentUserDep`` first), so the context is established when reserve() runs. We
308	        # read the ContextVar rather than importing CurrentUserDep here to avoid the deps -> db ->
309	        # idempotency import cycle (this module is registered from core/db at load time).
310	        tenant_id = get_current_tenant_id()
311	        if tenant_id is None:  # pragma: no cover - guarded routes always run authenticated
312	            raise ValidationFailedError(
313	                message="Idempotency requires an active tenant context",
314	                code="idempotency.tenant_required",
315	            )
316	
317	        # Read the raw body here and hash it (D-013). Starlette caches the body on request.body()
318	        # (request._body), so the route handler's own body parsing still works after this read —
319	        # the stream is not consumed out from under it. A replay with a different body therefore
320	        # produces a different hash and is rejected as key-reuse.
321	        request_hash = compute_request_hash(await request.body())
322	        await reserve(factory, tenant_id, self.endpoint, idempotency_key, request_hash)
323	
324	        context = IdempotencyContext(
325	            session=session,
326	            factory=factory,
327	            tenant_id=tenant_id,
328	            endpoint=self.endpoint,
329	            key=idempotency_key,
330	        )
331	        try:
332	            yield context
333	        except Exception:
334	            # Business work failed (D-013 fail-closed): the document was rolled back by run_in_uow
335	            # (the staged capture UPDATE with it), but the IN_PROGRESS reservation was committed in
336	            # reserve()'s SEPARATE session, so it would otherwise linger. Delete it in its own
337	            # committed session so the SAME key is immediately retryable, then re-raise — the app's
338	            # exception handlers turn the re-raised error into the proper envelope (verified: a
339	            # generic Exception still routes through _handle_unexpected_error to a 500 envelope).
340	            await _cleanup_reservation(factory, tenant_id, self.endpoint, idempotency_key)
341	            raise
342	        else:
343	            if not context.captured:
344	                # Forgotten capture: the handler returned 2xx without calling capture(), so the
345	                # reservation never reached COMPLETED. The 2xx response has already been sent (in
346	                # this build the business commit lives in run_in_uow inside the handler, BEFORE
347	                # this teardown — D-013's literal "teardown rolls back" assumed a deferred session
348	                # commit), so the response can no longer be changed. We delete the dangling
349	                # reservation so the key is retryable and log a server error — the missing replay
350	                # record is the signal a guarded route forgot its capture() one-liner. Deviation
351	                # from D-013's rollback-on-forgotten-capture is documented in DECISIONS.md.
352	                await _cleanup_reservation(factory, tenant_id, self.endpoint, idempotency_key)
353	                logger.error(
354	                    "Idempotent endpoint %r returned 2xx without calling capture(); reservation "
355	                    "cleaned up but no replay record was stored",
356	                    self.endpoint,
357	                )
358	
359	
360	# Type alias a guarded route annotates its captured-context parameter with, e.g.
361	# ``idem: IdempotentDep = Depends(Idempotent("finance.journal.post"))``.
362	IdempotentDep = IdempotencyContext
363	
364	__all__ = [
365	    "REPLAYED_HEADER",
366	    "Idempotent",
367	    "IdempotencyContext",
368	    "IdempotencyKey",
369	    "IdempotencyReplay",
370	    "IdempotentDep",
371	    "compute_request_hash",
372	    "reserve",

1	"""D-014 keyset (seek) pagination — never OFFSET.
2	
3	Cursor browsing is O(page) at any depth and stable under concurrent inserts (the ERP norm for
4	ledger/list browsing). Every list orders by a whitelisted sort column plus the PK ``id`` as a
5	mandatory unique tiebreaker (``ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC``), fetches ``limit + 1`` rows,
6	and emits ``next_cursor`` from the last RETURNED row only when the extra row arrived.
7	
8	**Cursor.** ``base64url(JSON)`` of ``{"v":1, "k":[last sort values..., last id], "s": sort-spec,
9	"q": filter fingerprint}`` — opaque to clients, validated server-side. ``v``, ``s`` and ``q`` must
10	match the current request (a cursor minted for one query/sort/filter can't be replayed on
11	another) → 400 ``pagination.invalid_cursor`` on any mismatch or tamper.
12	
13	**Seek predicate.** Written in the EXPANDED portable OR-form
14	``col0 < k0 OR (col0 = k0 AND col1 < k1) OR (... AND id < kN)`` (directions flipped per column for
15	ASC). D-014 mandates this expansion because SQLite lacks MIXED-direction row-value comparison —
16	``(a, b) > (x, y)`` only works when every column sorts the same way, and our lists mix ASC/DESC
17	freely — so the expansion is the only form correct on BOTH engines (verified: this project's
18	aiosqlite, 3.53, DOES support uniform-direction row-values, but the expanded form is used
19	unconditionally so a mixed-direction sort is never silently wrong).
20	
21	**Placement deviation.** D-014's letter puts ``paginate`` in ``core/db.py`` and the cursor codec
22	in ``core/schemas.py``. The keyset machinery (codec + fingerprint + expanded predicate +
23	CursorParams) is substantial and cross-cutting, so it gets its own flat core file per STRUCTURE
24	§8.5 ("one concept per file") — a justified core addition recorded in DECISIONS.md, the same way
25	core/money.py and core/custom_fields.py were. The ``Page`` envelope stays in core/schemas.py.
26	"""
27	
28	import base64
29	import binascii
30	import hashlib
31	import json
32	import uuid
33	from dataclasses import dataclass
34	from datetime import date, datetime
35	from decimal import Decimal
36	from enum import StrEnum
37	from typing import Any
38	
39	import sqlalchemy as sa
40	from pydantic import BaseModel
41	from sqlalchemy import Select
42	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
43	from sqlalchemy.orm import InstrumentedAttribute
44	
45	from app.core.exceptions import ValidationFailedError
46	from app.core.schemas import Page
47	
48	DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50
49	MAX_LIMIT = 200
50	_CURSOR_VERSION = 1
51	
52	
53	class SortDirection(StrEnum):
54	    ASC = "asc"
55	    DESC = "desc"
56	
57	
58	@dataclass(frozen=True)
59	class OrderKey:
60	    """One whitelisted sort column + direction. ``paginate`` always appends the PK as the final
61	    tiebreaker, so a list declares only its business sort columns (e.g. created_at DESC)."""
62	
63	    column: InstrumentedAttribute[Any]
64	    direction: SortDirection = SortDirection.ASC
65	
66	    @property
67	    def name(self) -> str:
68	        return self.column.key
69	
70	
71	def _sort_spec(order_keys: list[OrderKey]) -> str:
72	    """Stable string identity of the sort (``'created_at:desc,id:asc'``), embedded in the cursor
73	    so a cursor minted under one ordering is rejected if the request's ordering changed."""
74	    return ",".join(f"{key.name}:{key.direction.value}" for key in order_keys)
75	
76	
77	def _encode_value(value: Any) -> Any:
78	    """Serialize a sort-key value to a JSON-safe, round-trippable form. datetimes/dates go to ISO
79	    strings, Decimals to strings (exact, consistent with D-015), UUIDs to str; primitives pass."""
80	    if isinstance(value, datetime | date):
81	        return value.isoformat()
82	    if isinstance(value, Decimal):
83	        return str(value)
84	    if isinstance(value, bool | int | float | str) or value is None:
85	        return value
86	    return str(value)
87	
88	
89	def encode_cursor(key_values: list[Any], sort_spec: str, filter_fingerprint: str) -> str:
90	    """base64url(JSON) of the last row's key tuple + the sort/filter fingerprints (D-014)."""
91	    payload = {
92	        "v": _CURSOR_VERSION,
93	        "k": [_encode_value(value) for value in key_values],
94	        "s": sort_spec,
95	        "q": filter_fingerprint,
96	    }
97	    raw = json.dumps(payload, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
98	    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).decode("ascii")
99	
100	
101	def decode_cursor(cursor: str, sort_spec: str, filter_fingerprint: str) -> list[Any]:
102	    """Decode and validate a cursor, returning its key tuple. Any tamper, malformed payload, wrong
103	    version, or a sort/filter fingerprint that does not match the CURRENT request raises 400
104	    ``pagination.invalid_cursor`` — a cursor cannot be replayed on a different query (D-014)."""
105	    try:
106	        raw = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(cursor.encode("ascii"))
107	        payload = json.loads(raw)
108	    except (binascii.Error, ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
109	        raise _invalid_cursor() from exc
110	    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
111	        raise _invalid_cursor()
112	    if (
113	        payload.get("v") != _CURSOR_VERSION
114	        or payload.get("s") != sort_spec
115	        or payload.get("q") != filter_fingerprint
116	        or not isinstance(payload.get("k"), list)
117	    ):
118	        raise _invalid_cursor()
119	    return payload["k"]
120	
121	
122	def _invalid_cursor() -> ValidationFailedError:
123	    return ValidationFailedError(
124	        message="The pagination cursor is invalid for this query",
125	        code="pagination.invalid_cursor",
126	    )
127	
128	
129	def filter_fingerprint(*parts: Any) -> str:
130	    """sha256-prefix of normalized filter parts (D-014). Routers pass whatever WHERE inputs scope
131	    the list (status, date range, search term…); a different filter set yields a different
132	    fingerprint, so a cursor from one filtered view can't bleed into another. Empty parts → the
133	    fingerprint of an empty filter set, still stable."""
134	    canonical = json.dumps([_encode_value(part) for part in parts], separators=(",", ":"))
135	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:16]
136	
137	
138	def _coerce_key_value(column: InstrumentedAttribute[Any], value: Any) -> Any:
139	    """Coerce a decoded cursor value back to the column's Python type so the seek comparison binds
140	    correctly on both engines. datetimes/dates and Decimals were ISO/str-encoded; the rest are
141	    JSON primitives that bind as-is (SQLAlchemy adapts UUID/str columns from the str form)."""
142	    python_type = getattr(column.type, "python_type", None)
143	    if value is None or python_type is None or not isinstance(value, str):
144	        return value
145	    if python_type is datetime:
146	        return datetime.fromisoformat(value)
147	    if python_type is date:
148	        return date.fromisoformat(value)
149	    if python_type is Decimal:
150	        return Decimal(value)
151	    if python_type is uuid.UUID:
152	        # The PK tiebreaker is a UUID column; SQLAlchemy's Uuid type binds a uuid.UUID, not the
153	        # str it was cursor-encoded as, so re-parse it here (else the bind processor blows up).
154	        return uuid.UUID(value)
155	    return value
156	
157	
158	def _seek_predicate(order_keys: list[OrderKey], key_values: list[Any]) -> sa.ColumnElement[bool]:
159	    """Build the expanded OR-form seek predicate (D-014). For sort columns c0..cN with the values
160	    from the previous page's last row, the predicate selecting STRICTLY-AFTER rows is::
161	
162	        cmp(c0)
163	        OR (c0 == v0 AND cmp(c1))
164	        OR (c0 == v0 AND c1 == v1 AND cmp(c2))
165	        ...
166	
167	    where ``cmp`` is ``<`` for a DESC column and ``>`` for ASC. The PK tiebreaker is already the
168	    last OrderKey, so every distinct row is on exactly one side of the boundary — no skips, no
169	    duplicates, even when earlier sort columns tie. Expanded (not row-value) so mixed ASC/DESC is
170	    correct on SQLite too."""
171	    coerced = [
172	        _coerce_key_value(key.column, value)
173	        for key, value in zip(order_keys, key_values, strict=True)
174	    ]
175	    clauses: list[sa.ColumnElement[bool]] = []
176	    for i, key in enumerate(order_keys):
177	        equals = [order_keys[j].column == coerced[j] for j in range(i)]
178	        strict = (
179	            key.column > coerced[i]
180	            if key.direction is SortDirection.ASC
181	            else key.column < coerced[i]
182	        )
183	        clauses.append(sa.and_(*equals, strict))
184	    return sa.or_(*clauses)
185	
186	
187	def _apply_order(stmt: Select[Any], order_keys: list[OrderKey]) -> Select[Any]:
188	    return stmt.order_by(
189	        *(
190	            key.column.asc() if key.direction is SortDirection.ASC else key.column.desc()
191	            for key in order_keys
192	        )
193	    )
194	
195	
196	async def paginate[T](
197	    session: AsyncSession,
198	    stmt: Select[tuple[T]],
199	    *,
200	    order_by: list[OrderKey],
201	    pk: InstrumentedAttribute[Any],
202	    cursor: str | None = None,
203	    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
204	    filters: str = "",
205	) -> Page[T]:
206	    """Keyset-paginate ``stmt`` and return a ``Page[T]`` (D-014). ``order_by`` is the whitelisted
207	    business sort; ``pk`` (the model's id) is appended as the mandatory unique tiebreaker so the
208	    cursor is stable. ``filters`` is the router's filter fingerprint (see
209	    :func:`filter_fingerprint`) baked into the cursor. The single generic helper module routers
210	    use — they never hand-roll keyset SQL.
211	
212	    Fetches ``limit + 1`` rows; if the extra row arrives, the page is full and ``next_cursor`` is
213	    minted from the LAST returned row's sort-key tuple. The cursor (when present) is decoded and
214	    validated against this request's sort + filter fingerprint, then turned into the expanded-OR
215	    seek predicate that selects strictly-after rows."""
216	    if limit < 1:
217	        limit = 1
218	    keys = [*order_by, OrderKey(pk, SortDirection.ASC)]
219	    sort_spec = _sort_spec(keys)
220	
221	    seek_stmt = stmt
222	    if cursor is not None:
223	        key_values = decode_cursor(cursor, sort_spec, filters)
224	        if len(key_values) != len(keys):
225	            raise _invalid_cursor()
226	        seek_stmt = seek_stmt.where(_seek_predicate(keys, key_values))
227	
228	    seek_stmt = _apply_order(seek_stmt, keys).limit(limit + 1)
229	    rows = list((await session.execute(seek_stmt)).scalars().all())
230	
231	    has_more = len(rows) > limit
232	    items = rows[:limit]
233	    next_cursor: str | None = None
234	    if has_more and items:
235	        last = items[-1]
236	        next_cursor = encode_cursor(
237	            [getattr(last, key.name) for key in keys], sort_spec, filters
238	        )
239	    return Page(items=items, next_cursor=next_cursor, limit=limit)
240	
241	
242	def map_page[S: BaseModel](page: Page[Any], schema: type[S]) -> Page[S]:
243	    """Validate a service-layer ``Page`` of ORM rows into its wire schema — the one-line router
244	    epilogue for every paginated list endpoint, so the items/next_cursor/limit plumbing is never
245	    hand-rolled (and the envelope can't drift between endpoints)."""
246	    return Page(
247	        items=[schema.model_validate(item) for item in page.items],
248	        next_cursor=page.next_cursor,
249	        limit=page.limit,
250	    )
251	
252	
253	@dataclass(frozen=True)
254	class CursorParams:
255	    """Parsed ``?cursor=&limit=`` query params (D-014). ``limit`` is clamped to ``[1, MAX_LIMIT]``
256	    and defaults to ``DEFAULT_LIMIT``, so a client can never request an unbounded page. A router
257	    declares ``params: CursorParamsDep`` and forwards ``params.cursor`` / ``params.limit`` to
258	    :func:`paginate`."""
259	
260	    cursor: str | None
261	    limit: int
262	
263	
264	def cursor_params(cursor: str | None = None, limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT) -> CursorParams:
265	    """FastAPI dependency parsing the cursor/limit query params with the max-limit cap (D-014)."""
266	    clamped = max(1, min(limit, MAX_LIMIT))
267	    return CursorParams(cursor=cursor, limit=clamped)
268	
269	
270	__all__ = [
271	    "DEFAULT_LIMIT",
272	    "MAX_LIMIT",
273	    "CursorParams",
274	    "OrderKey",
275	    "SortDirection",
276	    "cursor_params",
277	    "decode_cursor",
278	    "encode_cursor",
279	    "filter_fingerprint",
280	    "map_page",
281	    "paginate",
282	]

1	"""FastAPI dependencies (D-008 get_current_user, D-007 production ContextVar setter).
2	
3	This is the ONE place that sets `current_tenant_id` for the request lifecycle from a
4	validated access token; the pure-ASGI middleware in app.main resets it in a finally
5	block so request A's tenant never leaks to request B on the same worker.
6	"""
7	
8	import uuid
9	from dataclasses import dataclass
10	from typing import Annotated
11	
12	from fastapi import Depends
13	from fastapi.security import HTTPAuthorizationCredentials, HTTPBearer
14	from sqlalchemy import select
15	from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, async_sessionmaker
16	
17	from app.core.audit import actor_user_id_ctx
18	from app.core.auth import decode_token
19	from app.core.config import get_settings
20	from app.core.db import get_session, get_session_factory
21	from app.core.exceptions import AuthError
22	from app.core.models import User
23	from app.core.rbac import current_permissions, resolve_permissions
24	from app.core.tenancy import current_tenant_id
25	
26	# get_session / get_settings are re-exported so routers depend on a single core.deps
27	# surface rather than reaching into core.db / core.config directly.
28	__all__ = [
29	    "CurrentUser",
30	    "CurrentUserDep",
31	    "SessionDep",
32	    "SessionFactoryDep",
33	    "get_current_user",
34	    "get_session",
35	    "get_session_factory",
36	    "get_settings",
37	]
38	
39	# auto_error=False: a missing/blank header must surface as the D-014 auth envelope
40	# (AuthError -> 401), not Starlette's bare 403 HTTPException.
41	_bearer_scheme = HTTPBearer(auto_error=False)
42	
43	# Annotated dependency aliases: the modern FastAPI idiom that keeps Depends() out of
44	# parameter defaults (ruff B008) and lets routers share one typed handle.
45	SessionDep = Annotated[AsyncSession, Depends(get_session)]
46	# The sessionmaker dependency (test-overridable like get_session). Job-submitting routers pass
47	# it to schedule_job post-commit so the runner opens its sessions against the SAME database —
48	# the app factory in production, the per-test engine's factory under the conftest override.
49	SessionFactoryDep = Annotated[async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession], Depends(get_session_factory)]
50	_CredentialsDep = Annotated[HTTPAuthorizationCredentials | None, Depends(_bearer_scheme)]
51	
52	
53	@dataclass(frozen=True)
54	class CurrentUser:
55	    """Resolved request principal (D-008/D-009). `permissions` is the effective key set
56	    resolved by RBAC (one join query, cached 60s)."""
57	
58	    user_id: uuid.UUID
59	    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
60	    permissions: frozenset[str]
61	    token_version: int
62	
63	
64	async def get_current_user(
65	    credentials: _CredentialsDep,
66	    session: SessionDep,
67	) -> CurrentUser:
68	    if credentials is None:
69	        raise AuthError(message="Missing bearer token", code="auth.invalid_token")
70	
71	    claims = decode_token(credentials.credentials, expected_typ="access")
72	    try:
73	        user_id = uuid.UUID(claims["sub"])
74	        tenant_id = uuid.UUID(claims["tenant_id"])
75	        claim_version = int(claims["ver"])
76	    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
77	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token") from exc
78	
79	    # Set the tenancy ContextVar FROM the validated token (D-007 production setter):
80	    # the user lookup below then runs under the token's tenant, so a tampered
81	    # tenant_id can only ever resolve a user that actually belongs to that tenant —
82	    # cross-tenant access is impossible. The middleware resets this in a finally block.
83	    current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
84	
85	    user = (
86	        await session.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
87	    ).scalar_one_or_none()
88	    if user is None or not user.is_active:
89	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
90	    if user.token_version != claim_version:
91	        # Stale token after a "revoke everything" bump (D-008).
92	        raise AuthError(message="Invalid token", code="auth.invalid_token")
93	
94	    # RBAC resolution (D-009): one join query, memoized 60s on
95	    # (tenant_id, user_id, token_version). Runs under the tenant context set above, so
96	    # the user_roles/role_permissions rows are already tenant-filtered.
97	    permissions = await resolve_permissions(
98	        session, user.id, user.tenant_id, user.token_version
99	    )
100	    # Serialization-time masking (D-009) reads this ContextVar; the middleware resets it
101	    # in a finally block alongside current_tenant_id so it never leaks across requests.
102	    current_permissions.set(permissions)
103	    # D-010 audit context: now that the principal is known, stamp the actor onto every
104	    # audit row this request writes. The middleware seeded it None (system) and resets it.
105	    actor_user_id_ctx.set(user.id)
106	
107	    return CurrentUser(
108	        user_id=user.id,
109	        tenant_id=user.tenant_id,
110	        permissions=permissions,
111	        token_version=user.token_version,
112	    )
113	
114	
115	CurrentUserDep = Annotated[CurrentUser, Depends(get_current_user)]

1	"""AtlasError hierarchy rendered as the D-014 error envelope by handlers in app.main.
2	
3	This file also owns the D-014 DB-guard translation: trigger-raised `ATLAS_*` tokens are
4	mapped to envelope codes here so the DB backstops surface through the SAME envelope as
5	service-level checks. Kept in this file (not a new core/db_errors.py) because the map is a
6	small dict and STRUCTURE §8.1 prefers extending an existing home; promote to its own file
7	only if the table grows past a screenful.
8	"""
9	
10	from typing import Any
11	
12	from sqlalchemy.exc import DBAPIError
13	
14	
15	class AtlasError(Exception):
16	    """Base for every error the API surfaces deliberately. Codes are machine-readable
17	    and dot-namespaced (generic: common.*; domain rules: e.g. finance.period_closed)."""
18	
19	    def __init__(
20	        self,
21	        code: str,
22	        message: str,
23	        status_code: int = 400,
24	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
25	    ) -> None:
26	        super().__init__(message)
27	        self.code = code
28	        self.message = message
29	        self.status_code = status_code
30	        self.details = details
31	
32	
33	class NotFoundError(AtlasError):
34	    def __init__(
35	        self,
36	        message: str = "Resource not found",
37	        code: str = "common.not_found",
38	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
39	    ) -> None:
40	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=404, details=details)
41	
42	
43	class ValidationFailedError(AtlasError):
44	    def __init__(
45	        self,
46	        message: str = "Validation failed",
47	        code: str = "common.validation_error",
48	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
49	    ) -> None:
50	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=422, details=details)
51	
52	
53	class ConflictError(AtlasError):
54	    def __init__(
55	        self,
56	        message: str = "Conflict with existing state",
57	        code: str = "common.conflict",
58	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
59	    ) -> None:
60	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=409, details=details)
61	
62	
63	class AuthError(AtlasError):
64	    def __init__(
65	        self,
66	        message: str = "Invalid credentials",
67	        code: str = "auth.invalid_credentials",
68	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
69	    ) -> None:
70	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=401, details=details)
71	
72	
73	class PermissionDeniedError(AtlasError):
74	    def __init__(
75	        self,
76	        message: str = "Permission denied",
77	        code: str = "common.permission_denied",
78	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
79	    ) -> None:
80	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=403, details=details)
81	
82	
83	class TenancyError(AtlasError):
84	    def __init__(
85	        self,
86	        message: str = "Tenant context missing or mismatched",
87	        code: str = "tenancy.context_missing",
88	        details: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
89	    ) -> None:
90	        super().__init__(code=code, message=message, status_code=403, details=details)
91	
92	
93	# --- D-014 DB-guard translation (trigger token -> envelope) --------------------
94	#
95	# Table-driven so future backstops (ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED, ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE,
96	# ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY) plug in by adding one row. SQLite RAISE(ABORT) surfaces as
97	# IntegrityError and asyncpg plpgsql RAISE surfaces differently, but both are subclasses
98	# of DBAPIError and both carry the token in str(exc) — so substring matching on the base
99	# class covers both engines (D-022 pins it on each).
100	#
101	# DEVIATION from D-014's literal table: D-014 maps ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY ->
102	# internal_error 500; PLAN 3.5 binds it to 409 / "audit.append_only" (an append-only
103	# write is a client-visible conflict, not an opaque server fault), so this map follows
104	# the task. Finance tokens below are pre-registered for PLAN 4 and keep D-014's codes.
105	DB_GUARD_TOKEN_MAP: dict[str, tuple[int, str]] = {
106	    "ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY": (409, "audit.append_only"),
107	    "ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED": (422, "finance.period_closed"),
108	    "ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE": (422, "finance.entry_immutable"),
109	    "ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY": (422, "finance.journal_unbalanced"),
110	}

113	def translate_db_guard_error(exc: DBAPIError) -> AtlasError | None:
114	    """Map a trigger-raised ATLAS_* token in a DBAPIError to an AtlasError, or None if the
115	    error carries no known token (then it is a genuine integrity/operational failure and
116	    the catch-all 500 handler owns it). Matching is on the full message text because the
117	    token is embedded in the raised exception string on both engines."""
118	    message = str(exc.orig) if exc.orig is not None else str(exc)
119	    for token, (status_code, code) in DB_GUARD_TOKEN_MAP.items():
120	        if token in message:
121	            return AtlasError(code=code, message=token, status_code=status_code)
122	    return None

209	    payment per due partner can blow the request budget at scale, so this returns 202 {job_id};

52	def dunning_level_for(days_overdue: int) -> int:
53	    """The dunning level implied by ``days_overdue`` given DUNNING_THRESHOLDS (PLAN 4.6):
54	    0 below the first threshold, else the count of thresholds crossed. Total; never raises."""
55	    level = 0
56	    for bound in DUNNING_THRESHOLDS:
57	        if days_overdue >= bound:
58	            level += 1
59	        else:
60	            break
61	    return level

195	async def _drain_and_dispatch(session: AsyncSession) -> None:
196	    """Pop buffered events FIFO and run their handlers, sharing ``session``. Handlers may
197	    publish more events (appended to the same buffer); we keep draining breadth-first up to
198	    MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW total dispatches, then raise EventCycleError. A handler raising
199	    propagates — run_in_uow's caller rolls the whole transaction back (D-011: no isolation).
200	    """
201	    buffer = _buffer(session)
202	    dispatched = 0
203	    while buffer:
204	        event = buffer.pop(0)  # FIFO: oldest first
205	        for handler in handlers_for(event.key):
206	            if dispatched >= MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW:
207	                raise EventCycleError(dispatched)
208	            await handler(session, event)
209	            dispatched += 1
210	    # Defensive: an event with no handler still counts toward nothing; a cap breach can
211	    # only happen above. Clearing the (now empty) key keeps session.info tidy.
212	    session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)

218	) -> None:

220	    dependency (core/deps), by seed.py and by CLI flows, so HTTP, seed and tests get
221	    IDENTICAL event semantics.
222	
223	    Sequence: run ``work`` (the business mutation that publishes events) -> drain the
224	    buffered events FIFO and run their handlers on the SAME session (so handler effects,
225	    e.g. a COGS journal, are in the same transaction as the trigger, e.g. the stock
226	    issue) -> commit. If the business work OR any handler raises (or the cascade cap is
227	    hit), roll the WHOLE transaction back and re-raise — the trigger's own writes do not
228	    persist. Handlers run under the trigger's active tenant context (D-007); nothing here
229	    changes it.
230	
231	    ``work`` may be a coroutine object or a zero-arg callable returning an awaitable, so
232	    both ``run_in_uow(session, service_coro)`` and ``run_in_uow(session, lambda: ...)``
233	    read naturally at call sites.
234	    """
235	    try:
236	        awaitable = work() if callable(work) else work
237	        await awaitable
238	        await _drain_and_dispatch(session)
239	        await session.commit()
240	    except Exception:
241	        await session.rollback()
242	        # Drop any partially drained / leftover buffer so the next uow on this session
243	        # (tests reuse one session) starts clean.
244	        session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)

"""Inventory stock topology + the move ledger + the maintained on-hand projection (PLAN 5.2).

This file owns the four STOCK tables (the master tables live in ``models/masters.py``):

- ``Warehouse`` / ``Bin``: the storage topology. A bin belongs to a warehouse; on-hand is tracked
  PER BIN. Both are reference data (codes, not gapless numbers).
- ``StockMove`` (``inv_stock_moves``): the quantity SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH (D-020). One append-only
  ledger row per movement, POSTED at creation and IMMUTABLE — corrections are reversing moves, never
  edits (the universal-journal philosophy of D-017 applied to stock). Quantity is ALWAYS POSITIVE;
  the ``move_type`` decides which of from_bin/to_bin participate (the direction), so no signed column
  is needed (constants.MOVE_BIN_SIDES). Carries DocumentMixin (registered in core_documents) and a
  gapless STK number claimed at creation (D-012 claim-at-permanence — a move is permanent at create).
- ``StockQuant`` (``inv_stock_quants``): the MAINTAINED PROJECTION of the move ledger — current
  on-hand per (item, bin, lot). Updated in the SAME transaction as every move (the moving-average
  ``inv_item_valuations`` precedent, D-020), so on-hand reads are an indexed point-lookup instead of
  an unbounded SUM over history (PERFORMANCE §1). The ledger stays the SSOT/audit trail; the quant is
  reconcilable from it. A DB ``CHECK (on_hand_qty >= 0)`` plus a pre-flight service check forbid
  negative stock outright (D-020) — both engines (a single-column CHECK is portable, D-022). Recorded
  as DECISIONS.md D-036.

Indexes (PERFORMANCE §1) are declared so the on-hand sums and the move-ledger filters are
index-served: moves index (tenant, item, to_bin), (tenant, item, from_bin), (tenant, move_date) and
(tenant, item); quants index (tenant, item) on top of the natural-key UNIQUE.

Enum-valued columns are plain ``sa.String`` storing the StrEnum's UPPER_SNAKE value (the
core/finance/masters convention); the service maps to/from the constants classes. Every table
follows the D-007 composite-tenant-FK backstop (``tenant_unique()`` + ``tenant_fk()`` composites).
"""

import uuid
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal

import sqlalchemy as sa
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from app.core.docflow import DocumentMixin, document_fk
from app.core.models import (
    AuditMixin,
    Base,
    TenantMixin,
    TimestampMixin,
    UuidPKMixin,
    tenant_fk,
    tenant_unique,
)
from app.core.money import QuantityType


class Warehouse(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """A physical or logical stock location grouping bins (parity: plant/storage location). ``code``
    is user-supplied and unique per tenant. ``is_active`` deactivates a warehouse instead of deleting
    it (a warehouse referenced by moves/quants must never disappear — the soft-delete convention).
    Audited (D-010): topology is master data. ``tenant_unique()`` so bins can reference it via the
    composite tenant FK."""

    __tablename__ = "inv_warehouses"
    __table_args__ = (
        sa.UniqueConstraint("tenant_id", "code", name="uq_inv_warehouses_tenant_id_code"),
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
    )

    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=False)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()
    )


class Bin(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """A storage bin within a warehouse — the granularity on-hand is tracked at (parity: storage
    bin). ``warehouse_id`` is a composite tenant FK to inv_warehouses (a bin can never belong to
    another tenant's warehouse). ``code`` is unique per (tenant, warehouse) — two warehouses may both
    have a bin "A1". ``is_default`` marks the warehouse's default receiving bin (a receipt that names
    only a warehouse can resolve to it later); exactly-one-default-per-warehouse is a service
    convention, not a DB constraint (a partial unique index is a later optimisation). ``is_active``
    deactivates instead of deleting. Audited (D-010)."""

    __tablename__ = "inv_bins"
    __table_args__ = (
        sa.UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id", "warehouse_id", "code", name="uq_inv_bins_tenant_id_warehouse_id_code"
        ),
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        tenant_fk("inv_warehouses", "warehouse_id"),
        # FK index for "this warehouse's bins" — the bins-list-by-warehouse read path.
        sa.Index("ix_inv_bins_tenant_id_warehouse_id", "tenant_id", "warehouse_id"),
    )

    warehouse_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    code: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(40), nullable=False)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(200), nullable=False)
    is_default: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=False, server_default=sa.false()
    )
    is_active: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()
    )


class StockMove(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, AuditMixin, TimestampMixin, DocumentMixin, Base):
    """The quantity SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH (D-020): one append-only ledger row per stock movement.

    POSTED at creation and IMMUTABLE — a move is never edited or deleted; a correction is a NEW
    reversing move linked via docflow (the D-017 reversal philosophy applied to stock). ``quantity``
    is ALWAYS POSITIVE; ``move_type`` (constants.MoveType) decides which of ``from_bin_id`` /
    ``to_bin_id`` participate (constants.MOVE_BIN_SIDES) — so direction is structural, not a sign.
    ``quantity`` is stored in the item's BASE UoM (``base_uom_id`` records which, frozen on the move
    so a later UoM change can't reinterpret history). ``lot_id`` / ``serial_id`` carry batch/serial
    identity for tracked items (NULL for fungible). ``reference`` is a free-text link to the driving
    document description (a real docflow link lands when receipts/issues drive moves, 6.x/5.3).

    DocumentMixin registers the move in core_documents; the gapless STK number is claimed AT CREATION
    (D-012 claim-at-permanence — a move is permanent the moment it exists, the orders/receipts
    branch). Audited (D-010): every quantity change is auditable. Indexes per PERFORMANCE §1 so the
    quant maintenance lookups and the ledger filters are index-served."""

    __tablename__ = "inv_stock_moves"
    __table_args__ = (
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        document_fk(),
        tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id"),
        tenant_fk("inv_uoms", "base_uom_id"),
        # from_bin / to_bin are both composite tenant FKs to inv_bins. The D-022 column-0 convention
        # would name both identically (collision), so spell out distinct names (the journal
        # self-FK precedent) — they must match migration 0021 exactly.
        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
            ["tenant_id", "from_bin_id"],
            ["inv_bins.tenant_id", "inv_bins.id"],
            name="fk_inv_stock_moves_from_bin_id_inv_bins",
        ),
        sa.ForeignKeyConstraint(
            ["tenant_id", "to_bin_id"],
            ["inv_bins.tenant_id", "inv_bins.id"],
            name="fk_inv_stock_moves_to_bin_id_inv_bins",
        ),
        tenant_fk("inv_lots", "lot_id"),
        tenant_fk("inv_serials", "serial_id"),
        # On-hand maintenance + ledger reads filter by item + bin and by date (PERFORMANCE §1):
        # the (tenant, item, to_bin) / (tenant, item, from_bin) indexes serve per-bin lookups, the
        # (tenant, move_date) index serves the ledger date filter, and (tenant, item) the
        # per-item ledger view.
        sa.Index("ix_inv_stock_moves_tenant_id_item_id_to_bin_id", "tenant_id", "item_id", "to_bin_id"),
        sa.Index(
            "ix_inv_stock_moves_tenant_id_item_id_from_bin_id",
            "tenant_id",
            "item_id",
            "from_bin_id",
        ),
        sa.Index("ix_inv_stock_moves_tenant_id_move_date", "tenant_id", "move_date"),
        sa.Index("ix_inv_stock_moves_tenant_id_item_id", "tenant_id", "item_id"),
    )

    move_number: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(60), nullable=False)
    move_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(sa.String(12), nullable=False)
    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    quantity: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)
    base_uom_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    from_bin_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    to_bin_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    lot_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    serial_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    move_date: Mapped[date] = mapped_column(sa.Date, nullable=False)
    reference: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(sa.String(500), nullable=True)
    posted: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(
        sa.Boolean, nullable=False, default=True, server_default=sa.true()
    )


class StockQuant(UuidPKMixin, TenantMixin, TimestampMixin, Base):
    """The MAINTAINED on-hand projection of the move ledger (D-036): current quantity per
    (item, bin, lot). Updated in the SAME transaction as every move (decrement from_bin, increment
    to_bin) so on-hand is an indexed point lookup, not an unbounded SUM over history (PERFORMANCE
    §1) — the moving-average ``inv_item_valuations`` precedent (D-020). The move ledger stays the
    SSOT; the quant is reconcilable from it.

    ``lot_id`` is part of the natural key (NULL for fungible/untracked stock — the same item+bin can
    hold several lots, each its own quant row). The ``CHECK (on_hand_qty >= 0)`` is the DB backstop
    behind the service's pre-flight InsufficientStockError, banning negative stock on BOTH engines
    (D-020; a single-column CHECK is portable, D-022). NOT AuditMixin: the quant is a derived
    projection, not independent business state — the MOVES that change it are audited, so auditing
    the projection too would double-record (the same reasoning core applies to derived/control
    tables). ``UNIQUE(tenant, item, bin, lot)`` is the upsert target; ``(tenant, item)`` indexes the
    total-on-hand aggregate."""

    __tablename__ = "inv_stock_quants"
    __table_args__ = (
        sa.UniqueConstraint(
            "tenant_id",
            "item_id",
            "bin_id",
            "lot_id",
            name="uq_inv_stock_quants_tenant_id_item_id_bin_id_lot_id",
        ),
        tenant_unique(),
        tenant_fk("adm_tenants"),
        tenant_fk("inv_items", "item_id"),
        tenant_fk("inv_bins", "bin_id"),
        tenant_fk("inv_lots", "lot_id"),
        # Bare token (the D-022 ck convention wraps it as ck_inv_stock_quants_on_hand_non_negative).
        # Negative stock forbidden outright (D-020) — exact on both engines (a single-column
        # comparison on the stored representation: NUMERIC on PG, micro-unit INTEGER on SQLite).
        sa.CheckConstraint("on_hand_qty >= 0", name="on_hand_non_negative"),
        # Total-on-hand-for-an-item aggregate (sum across bins/lots) is index-served (PERFORMANCE §1).
        sa.Index("ix_inv_stock_quants_tenant_id_item_id", "tenant_id", "item_id"),
    )

    item_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    bin_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=False)
    lot_id: Mapped[uuid.UUID | None] = mapped_column(sa.Uuid, nullable=True)
    on_hand_qty: Mapped[Decimal] = mapped_column(QuantityType(), nullable=False)

    # The datetime import is used by the inherited TimestampMixin's mapped columns at class build;
    # referencing it here is unnecessary but the annotation imports above keep ruff/mypy aligned.


__all__ = ["Bin", "StockMove", "StockQuant", "Warehouse"]

"""Warehouse business logic (PLAN 5.2): CRUD on the stock topology's top level.

Warehouses are reference data (codes, not gapless numbers). A warehouse is never hard-deleted —
moves and quants reference its bins, so deactivation (``is_active=False``) is the only removal path
(documented soft-delete convention). ``from __future__ import annotations`` keeps ``Page[Warehouse]``
(the ORM model) a string at import; the router re-validates page items.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid

from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from app.core.exceptions import ConflictError, NotFoundError
from app.core.pagination import DEFAULT_LIMIT, OrderKey, SortDirection, paginate
from app.core.schemas import Page
from app.modules.inventory.models import Warehouse
from app.modules.inventory.schemas import WarehouseCreate, WarehouseUpdate


async def _warehouse_by_code(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, code: str
) -> Warehouse | None:
    stmt = select(Warehouse).where(
        Warehouse.tenant_id == tenant_id, Warehouse.code == code
    )
    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()


async def get_warehouse(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, warehouse_id: uuid.UUID
) -> Warehouse:
    warehouse = await session.get(Warehouse, warehouse_id)
    if warehouse is None or warehouse.tenant_id != tenant_id:
        raise NotFoundError(
            message="Warehouse not found", code="inventory.warehouse_not_found"
        )
    return warehouse


async def create_warehouse(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: WarehouseCreate
) -> Warehouse:
    """Create a warehouse. Rejects a duplicate code (the DB UNIQUE is the backstop)."""
    if await _warehouse_by_code(session, tenant_id, payload.code) is not None:
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"A warehouse with code {payload.code} already exists",
            code="inventory.warehouse_code_conflict",
            details={"code": payload.code},
        )
    warehouse = Warehouse(
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        code=payload.code,
        name=payload.name,
        is_active=payload.is_active,
    )
    session.add(warehouse)

A bin belongs to a warehouse (validated to exist + active on create); its code is unique per

async def get_bin(session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, bin_id: uuid.UUID) -> Bin:
    bin_row = await session.get(Bin, bin_id)
    if bin_row is None or bin_row.tenant_id != tenant_id:
        raise NotFoundError(message="Bin not found", code="inventory.bin_not_found")
    return bin_row


async def _bin_by_code(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, warehouse_id: uuid.UUID, code: str
) -> Bin | None:
    stmt = select(Bin).where(
        Bin.tenant_id == tenant_id,
        Bin.warehouse_id == warehouse_id,
        Bin.code == code,
    )
    return (await session.execute(stmt)).scalar_one_or_none()


async def create_bin(
    session: AsyncSession, tenant_id: uuid.UUID, payload: BinCreate
) -> Bin:
    """Create a bin in a warehouse (PLAN 5.2). Validates the warehouse exists and is active;
    rejects a duplicate (warehouse, code). The DB UNIQUE + composite FK are the backstops."""
    warehouse = await get_warehouse(session, tenant_id, payload.warehouse_id)
    if not warehouse.is_active:
        raise ValidationFailedError(
            message="Cannot add a bin to an inactive warehouse",
            code="inventory.warehouse_inactive",
            details={"warehouse_id": str(payload.warehouse_id)},
        )
    if await _bin_by_code(session, tenant_id, payload.warehouse_id, payload.code) is not None:
        raise ConflictError(
            message=f"A bin with code {payload.code} already exists in this warehouse",
            code="inventory.bin_code_conflict",
            details={"code": payload.code, "warehouse_id": str(payload.warehouse_id)},
        )
    bin_row = Bin(
        tenant_id=tenant_id,
        warehouse_id=payload.warehouse_id,
        code=payload.code,
        name=payload.name,
        is_default=payload.is_default,
        is_active=payload.is_active,

    await session.flush()

) -> Bin:

    immutable and absent; ``is_active=False`` is the soft-delete."""
    bin_row = await get_bin(session, tenant_id, bin_id)
    data = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
    for field, value in data.items():
        setattr(bin_row, field, value)
    await session.flush()

async def list_bins(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    *,
    warehouse_id: uuid.UUID | None = None,
    cursor: str | None = None,
    limit: int = DEFAULT_LIMIT,
) -> Page[Bin]:

        pk=Bin.id,
        cursor=cursor,
        limit=limit,
        filters=filter_fingerprint(warehouse_id),
    )
